I was one of five Members asked to stand before the Democratic Caucus and help nominate Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker of the House. I told my colleagues about a foundational truth the Army teaches every soldier from day one: You do not choose the terrain you fight on, and you do not win a campaign with a divided platoon. You win through discipline, unity of command, and a leader who never leaves a soldier behind. Over the last two years, our Caucus has been tested under heavy fire. Yet time and again, we held the line, because we had a leader who kept his cool. Hakeem Jeffries does not lead from the rear. He has stood shoulder-to-shoulder with every wing of our Caucus, including frontliners in the toughest districts like mine. And every single one of us is coming back. Now the American people have handed us the high ground. They’ve given us a clear mission: lower costs for everyday families, restore accountability to Washington, and defend the democratic values that define this Republic. The job ahead is turning a hard-won victory at the ballot box into lasting relief at the kitchen table. **[The objective is clear and our ranks are formed. clean_body: | = = I was given an honor I’m still taking in. I was one of five Members asked to stand before the Democratic Caucus and help nominate Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker of the House. I told my colleagues about a foundational truth the Army teaches every soldier from day one: You do not choose the terrain you fight on, and you do not win a campaign with a divided platoon. You win through discipline, unity of command, and a leader who never leaves a soldier behind. Over the last two years, our Caucus has been tested under heavy fire. Yet time and again, we held the line, because we had a leader who kept his cool. Hakeem Jeffries does not lead from the rear. He has stood shoulder-to-shoulder with every wing of our Caucus, including frontliners in the toughest districts like mine. And every single one of us is coming back. Now the American people have handed us the high ground. They’ve given us a clear mission: lower costs for everyday families, restore accountability to Washington, and defend the democratic values that define this Republic. **TOP's Brianna Brown honored in The Root 100, Class of 2026** ** ** Read all about it: TOP is proud to announce that Executive Director Brianna Brown has been named as an honoree in [The Root 100!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143740687/661226763/1839657296?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNVE8vMS80NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MWU0NGJkNC03NmU0LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=rnVrGCRM4jibnHIlByjg2D4ugjm1H5guiyROA4caaog=&emci=5bf2b18c-5fe4-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=51e44bd4-76e4-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=227997) 🎉 Released each year, The Root 100 honors Black leaders across the country whose work and influence impacts lives and moves our communities forward. [View The Root's honorary shout-out of Brianna here, and share with your networks!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143740688/661226764/1839657296?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNVE8vMS80NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MWU0NGJkNC03NmU0LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=rnVrGCRM4jibnHIlByjg2D4ugjm1H5guiyROA4caaog=&emci=5bf2b18c-5fe4-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=51e44bd4-76e4-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=227997#brianna-brown)
**Celebrating historic Texas midterm wins with our communities** This past week in Houston, San Antonio, and Fort Worth, we celebrated the years of voter outreach, community organizing, and tireless movement building that brought us to this historic midterm. Texans voted for change in record numbers this election, and now it’s time for those leaders we helped elect to deliver it. Election Day wasn’t the finish line; it was just the beginning. At TOP, we organize year-round to hold officials accountable, so meaningful change can be delivered for Black and Latino Texans. Interested in learning more about our political work and getting involved? Email David at [dvillalobos@organizetexas.org](mailto:dvillalobos@organizetexas.org). **TOP offices closed next week** **TOP offices will be closed and staff will be off this coming week — Monday, Nov. 23 through Friday, Nov. 27** — to spend time with loved ones and rejuvenate after a busy election season. Our offices will re-open Monday, November 30.

**Español** **Brianna Brown de TOP, homenajeada en The Root 100, Clase de 2026** Brianna Brown de TOP, homenajeada en The Root 100, Clase de 2026 ¡Entérate de todo! TOP se enorgullece en anunciar que su Directora Ejecutiva, Brianna Brown, ha sido reconocida en [The Root 100.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143740690/661226766/1839657296?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNVE8vMS80NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MWU0NGJkNC03NmU0LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=rnVrGCRM4jibnHIlByjg2D4ugjm1H5guiyROA4caaog=&emci=5bf2b18c-5fe4-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=51e44bd4-76e4-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=227997) 🎉 The Root 100, que se publica anualmente, reconoce a líderes afroamericanos de todo el país cuyo trabajo e influencia impactan vidas e impulsan el progreso de nuestras comunidades. Durante más de 13 años, Brianna ha contribuido a definir la participación electoral de los texanos afroamericanos y a su organización para lograr un cambio transformador y audaz. Brianna es una organizadora nata que ha trabajado incansablemente para cambiar el rumbo político de nuestro estado y luchar por un futuro donde todos los texanos puedan prosperar. [¡Mira el reconocimiento de The Root a Brianna aquí y compártelo con tus contactos!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143740691/661226767/1839657296?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNVE8vMS80NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MWU0NGJkNC03NmU0LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=rnVrGCRM4jibnHIlByjg2D4ugjm1H5guiyROA4caaog=&emci=5bf2b18c-5fe4-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=51e44bd4-76e4-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=227997#brianna-brown)
**Celebrando las históricas victorias electorales en Texas con nuestras comunidades** La semana pasada, en Houston, San Antonio, y Fort Worth, celebramos los años de movilización de votantes, organización comunitaria, y construcción incansable de movimientos que nos llevaron a estas históricas elecciones de medio término. Los texanos votaron por el cambio en cifras récord en estas elecciones, y ahora es el momento de que los líderes que ayudamos a elegir lo hagan realidad. El día de las elecciones no fue el final; fue solo el comienzo. En TOP, nos organizamos durante todo el año para exigir responsabilidades a los funcionarios y así lograr un cambio significativo para los texanos afroamericanos y latinos. ¿Te interesa saber más sobre nuestro trabajo político y participar? Envía un correo electrónico a David a [dvillalobos@organizetexas.org](mailto:dvillalobos@organizetexas.org).
**Las oficinas de TOP cerrarán la próxima semana** Las oficinas de TOP permanecerán cerradas y el personal tendrá vacaciones la próxima semana, del lunes 23 al viernes 27 de noviembre, para que puedan disfrutar de tiempo con sus familias y recuperarse tras una ajetreada temporada electoral. Nuestras oficinas reabrirán el lunes 30 de noviembre.
**Consejos de TOP: Proteja sus datos personales tras estos últimos ciberataques** Esta semana ha sido caótica en cuanto a ciberataques contra algunos de los sitios web más visitados del mundo. Meet Coach Tuberville:
Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football’s 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville’s time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year’s Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP’s SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul “Bear” Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime.

Now, Coach Tuberville has been elected Governor of Alabama, and he’s ready to continue fighting for the people of his home state. His focus remains on protecting Alabama’s conservative values, strengthening communities, and keeping Alabama moving forward. Can he count on your support?_

### **Welcome to 907Honest.com**
---
---
**Looking for leaders in Anchorage, West Alaska, and Southeast. We are breaking the project into districts with Captains / Leaders per district.**

### **How will 2028 Differ from 2024 and 2026 efforts?**
**Ranked Choice Voting is so popular in Alaska that it took nearly $7 million of 99%+ out-of-state money just to squeak it through in 2020.** **It was so popular in 2024 that it needed ~$15 million (again, ~99% out-of-state) to barely survive a repeal.** **It was so popular in 2026 that it needed another ~$10 million (still overwhelmingly out-of-state) to defend the system.** **That’s $32 million+ of mostly Outside money poured into keeping Ranked Choice Voting alive in Alaska — plus the $50k settlement from the 2025 legal fight against my repeal effort.** **Get ready for another $15 million in 2028. They’ll need it. This time we will break the petitions into two parts.** **—————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————** **The original bill 19AKBE was three parts, it was campaign finance rules (Stop Dark Money), it was Jungle Primary (Open Primary), and it was Ranked Choice Voting (RCV).** **The 2024 Effort (My Effort) Noticed the Campaign Finance Language as a Poison Pill, so I removed it from the Repeal Attempt, they ran ads saying we were trying to give power back to the polticial parties, which was effective, the graphic above shows the result, very close loss even though we were winning for 2 weeks after election day and had a 4,000 vote lead on election day.** **The 2026 Effort (Establishment GOP) tried to repeal the whole 19AKBE and failed very badly even though they raised significantly more money than I did.** **The new Effort targeting 2028 will break the Open Primary and RCV into two bills and run them at the same time in simple language, easily translated, no campaign finance language included.**

Ranked Choice Voting is so popular in Alaska that it took nearly $7 million of 99%+ out-of-state money just to squeak it through in 2020. It was so popular in 2026 that it needed another ~$10 million (still overwhelmingly out-of-state) to defend the system. That’s $32 million+ of mostly Outside money poured into keeping Ranked Choice Voting alive in Alaska — plus the $50k settlement from the 2025 legal fight against my repeal effort. I'm Eduardo Verastegui. I produced the movie _Sound of Freedom_.

I'm so glad I found **you.**

Because the movie told one story. And there are so many more children waiting to be found.

Children like a young girl we'll call Kristen.

For months, she was locked in an attic.

No windows. No escape. Sold again and again.

**Until one day, she heard the sound of freedom. **

She knocked on a hotel room door.

She expected to find the person her trafficker had sent her to meet.

But when the door opened, Freedom Strike Force -- a rescue team we equip -- was waiting.

**She is safe today because someone cared enough to act**.

clean_body: Friend, I promise I won't take up much of your time. In my film 2000 Mules , I exposed one of the greatest scandals in American history - the hijacking of the 2020 presidential election. Today, I'm proud to join forces with Stand in the Gap, a non-profit organization dedicated to supporting the patriots who exercised their First Amendment rights in protest of the outcome of that election. I want to reach as many people as I can with this request... I told their founder, Shane Jenkins, that I would help him raise $20,000 before the end of the month to help Stand in the Gap provide help, hope, and healing to the January 6th patriots. Even a donation of $10 can give a January 6th patriot the support they need. Otherwise, let me explain why I 'm asking you to donate at least $10: $10 because the " crime" these patriots committed was fighting for their country. $10 because even though they've been pardoned, many of them are struggling to get back on their feet. $10 because Stand in the Gap is providing them with the resources they need to successfully reintegrate into their communities, find work, reconnect with family, and restore their rights. Not only are these men and women patriots, but they come from all walks of life -- law enforcement, veterans, white-collar professionals, blue-collar workers, and all races and religions. And they were hunted down in a political persecution that denied them their constitutional rights. Stand in the Gap exists to provide real, practical help, like rent money, job training, transportation, legal referrals, trauma counseling, and health insurance, to help these persecuted patriots move on with their lives. Your gift today can help one of these patriots find the help, hope, and healing they need to succeed in their second chance. Friend, can I count on you to contribute $10 or whatever you can afford to Stand in the Gap? Click any button below to give today. Thank you, Dinesh D'Souza P.S. name: Chris Deluzio
subject: One year ago: I wasn't scared ... but I was pissed.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Deluzio for Congress
body:
My initial reaction was, "what the hell is going on?"
# [](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/46?t=1&akid=173%2E42639%2EFxtw0N)
One year ago today, I got a call from my Chief of Staff telling me that Donald Trump had just called for my arrest, trial, and DEATH.
Remember this?
[](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/28?c0=deluzio-em-26-q4.4eyHU-&refcode=em261120&t=2&akid=173%2E42639%2EFxtw0N)
My initial reaction was, "what the hell is going on?"
But when I realized he was talking about the video five of my colleagues and I made my next thought was, "This f'ing guy has no understanding of the Constitution."
So what was that day like?
You saw the news, the aftermath ... but living through that day was WILD.
Our House office was immediately overwhelmed with calls. A lot of angry calls at first -- some very vicious, nasty and threatening. There were eventually bomb threats called into the office.
I wasn't scared ... but I was pissed.
We were in touch with law enforcement pretty quickly, and had to get security arranged at my house.
But as the day went on and news started getting out beyond people reading Truth Social, we got a lot of calls of support from inside the district and around the country.
I was in close contact with my five colleagues in the video over the course of the day.
We all responded forcefully, making clear that we were in this together -- not just for us, but for service members and for all Americans who could possibly find themselves under threat from the president if they said something he didn't like.
Remember, all of us in the video served in various capacities. We are pretty familiar with what happens in other countries when people dare to speak out against a leader. But that should not happen here, and we knew we had a responsibility to stand up against his attacks.
So we all issued our statements, communicated with supporters, there were some television appearances in the days that followed.
And that was the day...
Of course, it didn't end there. There were continued threats, there was an attempt to indict us, and even as recently as this weekend the president is still posting about us.
But today - I am reminded of the support from people like you in the aftermath and still... one year later. It meant a lot to me then, and it means a lot to me now.
Thank you. And remember: Don't give up the ship!
Chris Deluzio

* * *

☀️ Wait ... Before you click away! 🇺🇸
Here is the truth: Chris Deluzio is quite seriously considering running for John Fetterman's seat, but one of the things he'll have to know in advance is whether the support is there to take him on. Because if we do, we'll be taking on not only John Fetterman, but AIPAC, Trump, and an overwhelming amount of corporate money spent against us.
He is not asking you to donate millions of dollars. And there are many ways for you to say you'd like him to run for Fetterman's seat. But one thing he will see right now - as he thinks about this over the holiday - is what kind of financial support there is for his potential campaign.
We're not asking for a crazy amount, just a few bucks to help us fill the coffers after the last election and to prepare for whatever comes next.

[](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNjYsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABDmRrgMWQaTjOxbW0xvvdWF2KmgfIx2VFwMHdHMiUODONAeINSc2TUl4fWhrnHT1rxPt2eQIICfT7GM8o1D5XgL5IKw68-DVfde1de4)
__
---
_Arresting me alongside President Trump as innocent men.
Freezing my bank accounts.
Shredding my law licenses.
Seizing my assets._
---
**And now, I have to be brutally honest about where things stand...**
---
**... _I’m being pushed to the brink of bankruptcy._**
---
**That’s the Left’s goal: to use every form of lawfare in their quiver to bleed me dry and bankrupt.**
---
_This is nothing but the most savage form of retaliation for successfully defending President Trump as his former attorney._
---
**But you know what, Friend?**
---
_I’d do it all over again!_
---
**I’d rather lose everything than betray what I know to be true. I could never lie and say what I'm going through is a fair and honest process just to hang on to “earthly possessions.”**
---
_"_For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul_?" (Mark 8:36)_
---
**And while I stare down the threat of bankruptcy and the possibility of spending my last remaining living years in a prison cell in Arizona – where the President _legally_ cannot pardon me – I REFUSE to surrender the fight for my freedom.**
---
5 years ago, I was called a “DEAD MAN WALKING.” The media said I was cooked. They said there was _ZERO_ CHANCE I could survive this magnitude of legal warfare.
---
**Yet here I am, standing tall and ready to fight in the final battle for my freedom.**
---
But now, as I fight with all I’ve got, I have only one place left to turn to help me reach the finish line and secure my freedom: _good and honest Americans like _YOU.__
---
_Kind souls like you are the reason I’ve made it this far – and you will be the reason I declare victory in the final showdown for my freedom._
---
Friend, I understand this was probably the last thing on your mind today. I get it. And that’s why I always say that if you can’t afford to help me in this fight, please delete this message and carry on with your day. Don’t even think twice about it.
---

subject: BREAKING re BAAJA: Congress considering this bill is a betrayal of the will of voters.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee
body:
# [](https://act.janepac.com/go/30?t=1&akid=29%2E6803%2Ett8JkD)
🚨 The Senate just passed BAAJA — a dangerous bill that will speed up the construction of energy-guzzling data centers and make it easier for polluters to sue the government if they don’t get what they want. **This is the exact opposite of what Americans voted for in the midterms. But we’re not letting up, not one bit. We’ve got to show those in power that when they do not act with our interests, we will hold them accountable.** **[Send a letter to your House representative right now and urge them to vote NO on this bill.](https://act.janepac.com/go/57?source=em20261120-29&t=3&akid=29%2E6803%2Ett8JkD)** **[WRITE MY LETTER ››](https://act.janepac.com/go/57?source=em20261120-29&t=4&akid=29%2E6803%2Ett8JkD)**
---
The Senate just pushed through the so-called Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA). It’s heading to the House _right now_. If the bill passes, it will gut bedrock environmental laws and unlock a new generation of fossil fuel infrastructure — and frustratingly, _some Democrats are leading the charge_.
**[Can you send a letter to your House representative right away and urge them to vote no on this dangerous legislation before it’s too late?](https://act.janepac.com/go/57?source=em20261120-29&t=5&akid=29%2E6803%2Ett8JkD)**
**[WRITE MY LETTER ››](https://act.janepac.com/go/57?source=em20261120-29&t=6&akid=29%2E6803%2Ett8JkD)**
_After you write your letter, you’ll be prompted to call your representative. Taking both actions will make a huge difference!_
This bill is a massive handout to fossil fuel executives, mining corporations, and Big Tech.
It allows them to bulldoze environmental safeguards, undermine Tribal sovereignty, and make it harder for local communities to challenge polluting projects in their own backyards.
Worse, it gives the Trump Administration carte blanche to rubber-stamp new drilling projects for the next two years.
**Let us be clear: BAAJA isn’t a compromise — far from it.** It changes the role of our government from protecting the public from corporations to protecting corporations from oversight.
And just think about the timing. Americans went to the polls only weeks ago and voted for the exact opposite of this bill. But its backers are racing to pass it _before_ the new Congress is sworn in this January – denying our JanePAC climate champions a chance to vote against it.
**So we have to put pressure on Congress the way we know how: with your voice. No more sneaky backroom deals with Big Oil. No more quietly peddling cruel legislation. Enough is enough.**
**[The best action you can take today is sending a letter to your representative in Congress to vote NO on BAAJA. Demand they say NO to corporate handouts and protect our planet.](https://act.janepac.com/go/57?source=em20261120-29&t=7&akid=29%2E6803%2Ett8JkD)**
**[WRITE MY LETTER ››](https://act.janepac.com/go/57?source=em20261120-29&t=8&akid=29%2E6803%2Ett8JkD)**
Congress considering this bill is a betrayal of the will of voters. Coming right off the results of the midterm election, the blue wave across the country shows that there is a huge mandate for change.
If there is any time to act boldly, it’s now. **We can’t go back to business as usual.**
Thank you for being in this fight with us.
Team JanePAC

Our historic win last Tuesday didn’t happen by luck. It was the result of
over a year of hard work from thousands of
supporters
just like you knocking doors, calling their neighbors, or chipping in a

Now, the hard work begins.

It’s time to build that Michigan. The only way we can make a Michigan

That’s the exact kind of leadership she will bring to the governor’s

name: Josh Shapiro
subject: My dad taught me something important
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY SHAPIRO FOR PENNSYLVANIA]
body:
[ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek,

My dad has been a pediatrician for decades.
Growing up, I wanted to follow in his footsteps and become a doctor myself
— until I nearly failed out of organic chemistry.

I remember vividly as a kid, the phone ringing in our house at all hours
of the night with a worried parent on the line — living through those
terrifying moments when you would trade anything just to know that your
child is going to be OK.

Hearing those conversations, my dad taught me something important: What
mattered more than what my dad said was what he didn’t say. He listened.
He offered more than a prescription — he offered a conversation.

That’s exactly what we did on the campaign trail for ten months. And
Derek, it’s exactly
what I’ll continue to do as your Governor here in Pennsylvania.

This might come as a shock to Donald Trump and JD Vance, but folks here in
Pennsylvania, and all across the country for that matter, don’t always
care what an elected official has to say. They care what elected officials
do.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/23754?t=1001&akid=971%2E245147%2EIrdWUt ]That’s why I couldn’t be more ready to roll up my sleeves and Get Stuff
Done with our Democratic majority — but I need your help to make the most
of it. Please, will you chip in just $5 or whatever you can right now to
make sure we kick off this brand new era of leadership on the right foot?

## NC Farmers Advise Getting Trees Early
North Carolina Christmas tree farmers are [_warning of higher prices_](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkDGOgzAQAF9jd0HejW2gcHENXa69Em3sBSw5gBYLlN-fcl-4ejRTzM9jfFAueZ2_6cVhWuO48nUUrpVlnLlWYT6YpLyFCud5iYvkY0SD_gZwQzPush07xzqCTqFt775PmgO0vYMWewN6CS4yeX6SN8m51vvokmNGxzQ9U3Koc_gEAdAAmA76Bpy1ZgLqrMXueQdlDadcN2mm8t5OlnWTukSSreSVmri9dAlLrfuh7l8KB4XDdV3NJVQ-UOFAEpd8ssIB-r6znXEKBy0h7VcuJR--VdbML8p_gq7_fXEG_A0AAP__MmNy6w) and shortages this year because fewer trees were planted a decade ago, and urge customers to buy early as supplies may sell out quickly. Workers at Cornett Carolina Trees in Vilas [_cut about 1,000 trees_](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkLGO5CAMhp-GdIywwwRSUFyTbq-9MvIQJyARGAG7o3n7U-YVtrELW7--__v3tX5RTDEff-lkt2e_Zn61xL1zXQ_uvTI3pprelRLHI_hQY1tR4SQBJKr1WUt7su8rDJszZpzmbWAHZr6DwVnBENxjs8Yi3CeFPM12R03jYyav7yNb4-0Q3RUIgApAWZhvcNda7UBWa7SPEYRWvMVe6m1P7_LDNZfag6daUsx08-Uckgu9P5sY_whcBC4fqPp9puIpXaWuL4FL9gKXXiPlI7FslLcQU2rXhV_XulAELgDXMAKXT-V-UpMfG5Iqy1xeMjBtMR-y7LvsgeVZvnOnmIfqtucrphTbZIRWx0kxfRj7bw3_OPwfAAD__y6zkVo) daily and ship them nationwide to destinations including Chicago, Florida, and New Orleans. The owners note that demand has shifted earlier over the past decade, with many buyers seeking trees before Thanksgiving, and said they expect to be able to fulfil demand this season. Boone farmers say families are [_arriving sooner_](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkLGuqzAMhp8mbKniEKAMGe7C1rveEYVgIKpJUOLbqm9_lL7CWWzJ_mV9_v495ocLFOL-151ot-jniO9CyIx53pE5IxZ0mT7ZEYb98EcOZdZK9xJAajVfOZULPc_QrHYY2n5cG7QwjB0MelTQHBaU39yiOqOWZTUtOje2w9b2sCns27Frgq0HAbQCUHcYb9AZozZwd2P0fWlBGIVr4JRvG33SC3NMmQ_vcqIQ3c2nsyF7MF9FtH-EnoSevlD5_0nJO6pP1ZTQU_RCT5yDizuhLC6uRyAqdYPv2iqK0BNALUMNu2eIu-QDJYcTJSd5Bf_8Di7MG3qW1VOT7Xq9A1Eo_SCM2k8X6MvGvzX7svonAAD__wN8jmY) to choose their own trees, with some saying they like to put up their trees earlier to extend the Christmas spirit. Farms report the early rush is common, and trees can last through New Year’s with proper watering.

The Virginia State Crime Commission voted to recommend a [$5,000 civil penalty per violation](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGupDAMRb8GuqA4BMIUKbahm223RCaYGUuBoGAF7d8_MZo_eKV9pKtz77_n9ESOvL_-4kZeyjrtdJ2RRChPR0ShTLhQjryxnHtAvNJGk9GmVwDK6AmDcKHJYr34FS3hoyYP7tGBa6Ez9dsvAdA4M7c9QDeg03ZwXW8fYPW8LgA1-zsPwGgAMK1uqHUr6ZkGa53W81BZTQtLyo28qXB-8c64xv-pUG5C2uro3yLHWbV_KjNWZryuq7mkfGBlxrtTZcaYAkb1PUoIKlNI20b7gsJpP2-kMB5ZZTolc_h-U1EwqNuxzn45Lo6Rz95VVr825PgxkF-OV7z5CQAA__-LCoUE) for police agencies that misuse automated license plate readers, with each unlawfully shared record counted separately. Part of a package headed to the 2027 General Assembly, the proposals would also allow random state audits of agency programs by the Department of Criminal Justice Services, require data requests in writing[,](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkDuO3DAQRE9DZT3gT8PdgIETZevUodCiWqMG-BFIjgZ7e0Nj-ASbVPRQVXh_vuYv5Mj58RsT-X5uc6ZXi9Q71fmI2KkSrlQjJ-4tB8RXSTRrqe-gFGg5Y-h80mxxWP2GlvBzIK_c56icUaMedj-6sOiFRoXj6oKx2tzvbkSL0ilrdBjYX31KaamU0kbeyLiN5EIf1joplw9hJa3cS731nU6uD86MW_wuJ9VbKGmIfu_9aML8EnoSevrPJKrhWb8vRujpWhF6UuoKc2EIoXIiODBThEqhpER5bdDL87FThYMyxs7UYCsVIgfKjeAtBv6ZgcTt2QhaL0eDtpfaoWywYBZ6GqpfjxfHyO3uhJWPhBzfj_sPZZ9e_w0AAP__5LqWIg) and bar sharing plate data for immigration and health care enforcement without a court order. The recommendations followed a [commission survey](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkMFq-zAMxp_GudVYSlI3Bx96-Af-0JZRGDsGx1ZSgxMHx0vY24947Al20feJT_wk9HHv7tp5N48PPZFK29DNtK-eUqLYLV4niqQtRe8ml9bZaL2HiToUeD4BnFB02iS3UVfpwqpBV6SbghTIpgZZQo3FS4mmJiLZgzUAdSMl0EX3dX0mC1T1WDh18ABQAACWglMpBxI9XapKCtFfWCXIuhQiTy_aXBzd7PTgv8JGkZswFV69UlpWVl4ZtgzbbTWG_w7yMWwMWxvM50RzWhm2xz6GNYqb3rP-m4cQDR157q-3t2c27ytlfdIS4k92yrX9_7jesgPgyA8iX-xQRGWX3Xnv1rNklRgn7Xy-Mf3xvZvC7wAAAP__htKJYg) published this month in which 20 of 191 responding agencies reported misuse, though only two cases led to charges. ## UVA Study Targets an Alzheimer’s Gene
University of Virginia researchers found that [a gene called CASS4](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkDGuozAURVcDnSPbkEAKF9PQZdop0QNf8NMYg-w3oMzqv_K38MsrXR0dnT-v8UUcOa2_aYOTcxkTrhIhgjwekQQZ5JEjbywlzUTXvmG02j6UMcrqkWbhE2NLtXcLtaBnDWe65910jbnbOrjG-MV0XjfTvPSAt83dd8a2RuuenqCa3YdnjNXGGNvoG5pugZ7Qt22n9dRXrYZn2fNNAk7OKyemJb73E_k271sdXRA5StX8quxQ2aHMLJiDJ47vz6GyA8X_AbwhFzVl0F8Jef-3BpVxgmJRVyBRgY4D6TOQlASoKROnouYISpxWVd5FsKmFOJbKDnV2_rg4Ri6Prmr1uhHHbyP5YczT2a8AAAD__0nEjcU) directs the brain’s immune cells to contain the toxic plaques linked to Alzheimer’s disease. In lab mice, the [_UVA Health team showed_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuhDAQBNCvgc7IXjgMhYs0dJc2JVrMAisZc7IdW5evj8gvpB-90czXc34iO_b7J55kUt5mTyU6SonC_HKYKBCuFByfnKK3iOU6aQYJvVBKgJzRJs40d1ivZsOOcKzJKD0-lG7VA-rDaLsOY281DRq3Ftt1tDD0HahRjyAXW7O5PaVAKqWglQ21eiO50NB1WsplqDpJK6crNOmgzGFnz7i595UpNPY6a2eOlF6xaj8qmCqYSinNd8aD0KXjTlQw3cMqmND9HMQnBRHFytHexlsEyoQuiiUge2EdoWe_i_3yJEq4_F4Hs74KO8ex11Un9xPZ_XWnf96WDfwGAAD__9Q_hQo) that when CASS4 malfunctions, immune cells called microglia can no longer compact amyloid-beta plaques. The plaques then build faster, damage neurons, and drive cognitive decline. The finding, published in the [_Journal of Experimental Medicine_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAQgOGnMVvQ3dmBMHjowpauHdGBz-QqgyNjEfXtq_QV-gLfL_1f9-nOmnRfP3kTX8847fI6ktQqZXomrlKEg5Skm9ZjX5hfeZOJgLoL4oVg4qXqKZPjJvjITnhoxGM_XLG3eKXm4QcHsxuiXRx1FMh29jpIJJmjmwMEadS_PUQCRCQLrdg-Csxyc64HmG_GgQStubT1IaeWVXflmH7yKaVd8tYk_6j1eRj7YWg0NIasbS6roRGhRbg5Q-O3bO27AwiuKT48X5qSHl1vHKwba_qT6j8nnJ5-AwAA___p4m6B), challenges a common assumption that the gene works through nerve cells. Lead researcher John Lukens said it acts mainly through the brain’s immune system. Lukens said strategies that boost the gene could offer “a much-needed approach” to treating a disease that affects [_roughly 7.4 million Americans_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0DturTAQgOHVmM7ILzAuXNyG7tw2JRrsMYxkHjIOKGf1UbKFbODXr-_jNb2AMu3Lf9jQ1ztNOz5XxlqxTGeGigUhYsm0Ub32APAcG05KqJ5LyZWYIFS6cTLQRJ_AILgGvbSuk1bLTjWrD6ZzSXZO6eBmcDElmI0Ws51hCEJBQ_6nJ6USUkqlRYvaJhQzDsZYIeaBGYGR6lHauuJNZaGdIOWv48bShmNrsl9rPS-m_zE1MjU-z9NCfrdHWZgaF6wbRgKmRkxDMkNyHKLuuRkQ-GCT47M1Qpted0EiUyPk94q0Ybl4glAvDnvkiZbPgld7xtQUH8-Hcqart8yIZQPKvyf1j4i3V98BAAD__yzJhew). The research is early, and any therapies it points to have not been tested in people.

In lab mice, the that when CASS4 malfunctions, immune cells called microglia can no longer compact amyloid-beta plaques. The plaques then build faster, damage neurons, and drive cognitive decline. ## GOP Group Seeks State Surplus Refunds
Lawmakers with the state Freedom Caucus [asked](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSpiAQhJ9GMywG-EUCg0vM9tILrVEGpRbFgtn17u2v_F9h467u-r7-8zF_YEzx3H7jQSNvYT7promYqcyDXSojU_0qV_qqV05xpRxCnJVUvQAQSs5XyfWilWdo_ailJzBDSyNY9wKrwel2H9GZVQ_Qq8VLXK0OHjwE1xtJzi3atXF8FgGUBAANqlM9vIwLSq1hcdqFxkjykXPpeKeNctkihvQvf1Pp1ny0adyZr9roX42aGjXd993d4e_2hI2aHqlGTW-bRk0J7wM_qVRx48ni4Y-YRKVaYz4F7oRe5CCWzJyPKhg_47mJR319-lg4rolmYywGF4JYgpXitdhBuJdBoRforbXBOC-7nY_UltFfd0wp1t42Rm4HxvQG55-e_j2q_wEAAP__X-eW-A) Gov. Brian Kemp to call a special session before Gov.-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms takes office so lawmakers can return some surplus money to taxpayers. The state reported $8.7 billion in general fund reserves as of June 30. State Rep. Charlice Byrd, R-Woodstock, said the Republican group wants checks sent to taxpayers who paid into the system, though an amount hasn't been proposed. Kemp has [left open](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkDty8yAUhVeDOjzciyxZBcXfqPPfptTwuMiMkWEAWcnuM068g7RnvvOY83FdrjrE8Fj_641UW_3yoKNGao3KchlNbbpR3UuOe80pBkvJ-7CgwIEDcBRLLqlmsm2BzikpHEF_6UjBOJ1hlDDJ7qY0eGFGg-TE6Aa0whlpYRq0g0mORnRBvRIBUACABDzhAOd-8ojWm0lOnvWCXGipnNqNVkplDdrHr_SkcrJp66K6tZYrk_8YzgznN1LIpuJ-GYbzq4ThDMBwFj3D-U5b5kd6NG51jPzt4lEfm75Tqdxoe-ct8UKu6INvOleeykuxezGcPsnuLTyJ53RQqQznriiXjxBjqMPIerFuOsSfje2v_z4VfgcAAP__RPCQ7g) the possibility of a session on unspecified budget issues. The caucus also backs redrawing district lines, but Kemp [said](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkMFuhCAQhp8GbxgGXF0PHHrxtr32aBAHlxSFwKy0b9_Y9A16nUm-fN__8Zgfxgd_bO9mR02bmw-sJSAR5vk-LIUMYXnlFF4lxeAtRuf8LIXsOQCXYk45loSWZmhWrcSK0N0b1DCMNxgUjKp56r4bcBFgLFpYO7eAu48g1SBALMugROP1RQSQAgAUyFb2cOtGJ6V1y6hGxzqBq6eYW3rihjFv3rjwHU_MrY17E_STKBWm3picmJxqra1dyhVz_ZmcDAVzkGFyuo5MTls8-Sfuidd4ELcmBH6FeBN4wVJ8PDhFHvzuieMX2hf5E3mKFXPhMfOMazaV_8nw3aSL2mS9pupD8KUfWCe23fjwq0j_nffU8icAAP__DeWSvw) after the Nov. 3 election that he would not call a session to redraw maps.
## College Enrollment Sets Record
Enrollment in the state's public colleges and universities [rose](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkM2K2zAURp9G3ilY13_Rwot2IZgWl07aYSAbI1tXtkC2jHQTkbcvKXmDWX98B875HMZBO-_25ZfesKfFjjvm5JEI43jupkSaMN3i4W_pCN7NGKx1I5TQciE4lOMRQzpwplEUpq9Kg6I-F9iLTjaiq4SsirU_GwMwN6aZsLKN7MDWsm1RGDmhnUAWrn8ShYBSCFEJOEErmlpagNlOspKW1SUaRyGeaMUFQ1yctv4R7hhPc9gK369ER2LVNwaKgco5n3Ka6P5cGainFQPlw6w9A6XJ6500A3Xb3R1jcvTg6ZEIN_6i84hHiJR4xDlEw3GPwfsNd-I1rfyBOr4e2RnkSwyZVgZq-Lj8_HFpP9_U9-Hy-6rer3_em7e_1-GDgSpib47svHep7VhdLpt2_r8AfTX-vYd_AQAA__8pM5y2) 2.7% this fall to a record 392,581 students, the fourth straight year of growth. Enrollment grew at 21 of the 25 colleges and universities in the University System of Georgia, despite out-of-state enrollment falling 1.9% and international enrollment slipping 0.5%. Middle Georgia State University in Macon [posted](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uhDAQhJ8GOiPWNj8uXKShu7QpEZg1WFowspdD9_bRnfIGqUczo-_7eYyPKVA41u9pR8urHw-8MyEzprHv5swTY77SSVc-IwWH0fswylq2AkDIejxTzCc6HqFcrKoXBN2XaKEzDXQKjCo3q7SRqp19t5h5Vr5v-hqcVq6BVk-zacpg34sAsgYABbKSLTTaeCmdn40yvtA1LoFjqnjDFWNaw-TpFZ-YKhf3kuzGfOZCfRVyKORw33el4ZjdOy3ksIdlIRR_TfHBEtcRnphy4Jdw23Q4JIopC3edAo8UiXY8WKwp3rwVciiTXc47EIXcdoWu130K9Hnn_5p7WvkbAAD__27DhQw) the largest percentage increase of 14.1%, reaching a record 10,070 students. Georgia Tech [remained](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOtSAURleDHYZ7RdCC4m_s3t9OaXh6QRIUA_jM7H7ibGE28H3nnK_X_LIhhsP_tzuZ6t180F0i1Up5HvS7VFupXPmMVzlTDAsl58KMAhUH4CjmM6dy0lJnaFbTiZVADg0Z0GMPuoOxazZDMOAge6tQW2URHUrhLCyql0JorZpgnkUAFADQAbaooJejQ1zce-xGx6SgNdSU27qRp5R9sC5-pw_ldkl7E81W61lY94_hxHC677u9im9pvRhOjxPDKVMkW4jhdBXP6cgpxp2OysuVPRVeE8-0pLzyLfiNP0gMpyab9bxDjKEozaTwuw3x97T-NdjH4E8AAAD__5Wqf28) the largest campus with 58,264 students.
## _Idol_ Picks Filming Location
_American Idol_[announced](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkM2OnDAQhJ_G3DxyNyw_Bw4TKSjJavOzWWWOyJg2tGTGyO4F5e2jifIGOZdUVd93exlfLAe-L1_tRr0sfrzTmQOJUBrbZspihfJ72sN73mNgR9F7HtFgrQE0mnFPMe_kZIRi7kszE1RtQT003RM0JXRlsfauLqvW1xZqDwQtdtR0MLUGJmNnML7g_tEIgAYASsAL1vBUdR7R-akrO68qQzNLTBdZaaGYFrY-_I4HpYuLWxH6VWTPqrwqHBQO53lezjzJ8UgVDg8qhUOIzgaFg90osbN3zXMMOlMgJ1lL4sCy6sAHaZas73TqNW6k_y0qHKq32_Vb_dz8-vLp-fXz9frxw-vPob69ff-hcChSP-8nh8C5blRlls1y-PtP_tft0eOfAAAA__-mN44v) Trilith LIVE in Fayette County as the filming location for its 25th season, after deciding earlier this year to move the show's production from Los Angeles to Georgia. The season will premiere Feb. 8, and the 530,000-square-foot venue [will host](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uhDAQRk8DnREzmB8XLtLQbdqUyMAYRjIY2bNLcvtoc4X0n76n974e08Nx4HP7dAdZ2fx00p0DiVCahn7O4oTyM13hma8YeKHoPU9YY6cAFNbTlWK-aJEJytU29Uqgh5Is9KaFvgHTlLvVM-pVm8EM0Bvsdd8ubl1gJtJz181tyfb9CIA1ADSAFXbQauMRFz-bxvhC17SyxFTJThvFtLHz4Se-KFVLPMpgd5ErF81HgWOB433flY_frZPgTnHvTYHj263A0R2UeHGn4jUGxVnNic-Nz02xZIWt7CqTy_FUkjiw7Crwi8pk1-vmEDh3faHr7XAc_uDy33Avi78BAAD__-PJhF0) its live shows. [United States Tungsten](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkE2OHCEMhU9TtesWBupvwSLSqHeTbZaIAVNtiQIErh7l9lHNRLlAtn6f_Ozv17t9d5Qo7z_dgYb3aDN-9oTM2Oy6fHR2jP1sNZ29lkQeS4xkpZDzDeAmha2t9IqeLYzBKBEQ9DqigWWbYFGwqfFp_Ap6ntQitF-j9HILuKGHaZ1EkEr7kcy1EUAKAFAg73KGSW9RSh8_NrXFQQsMxKXd-Yk7lraTi-l3eWG7-3KMyTyZax_Uj0E-Bvmg_MLO9zMTY_h-gs-8d8Z88RekHicftpezeRzUGx6O0iDna3hgoPMY1Ft1FG7VNc7Y-pPq39y7ozra8xfxL4RV3LRY7LeXq9pZNQslVq0ErGMzoX5SStTnZdBivwq_juf_Ff8y8k8AAAD__wJOmNc) has plans to capitalize. ## Fiona the Hippo Dies at 9
Fiona, the Cincinnati Zoo’s hippo who drew fans around the world after her premature birth, [died Thursday at 9](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkDGvrCAUhH-NdhgOomhB8Rq7fe0rDcJhPQkCQXbNu7_-xu1ufcvJTCbzzb_H-jAUKD7_mgN1TbtfI15nwFqxrAUPPDYsFJ-eUjQ2RYsmoFsFFyMDYIKvuaQzo60rtE5L7MHPLWpQ8wCq72Fud-254bO0DoyZJu9HA4MDCWoQZhhxki3puxBAcAAYQHbzJJTbRrV5O-GEppEcHdVUurpj2in58D-9sXQ2HW3Qe635bPo_jVgasVzX1cXN3iC334glp8zsK9RXwZ-K3aFGLB88tlPOiTnCk1mKlmI0ldhXSqzYaEbgYlZt0S5fFAKdo2okfx6GwmdG_fV_by2-AwAA__8O64e7) after swallowing a knit hat, the zoo said. A child tossed the hat into the air Nov. 8, and an overhead fan [sent it into her enclosure](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOtCAURp8GO4wXUbCg-Bu7-dstDcJ1vAmCwZsxu0-_mXmFrb_kOznn67E8PCXKz__-QMdl35aM95WQGetS8cBjxUr5uVHJPpQc0CeMi-rUKAGk6pazluvEwAs00WnsYZsadGCmAUzfw9TsTg_GjnFF3GDUymqvB2thMOu0ad1p35B7HwKoDgAG0O1klYnraNYtWLTohe4wEpfa8o5lp7Kl7_LC2oZyNMntzOcl-n9CzULN9323d7r5PQo1-8oUEgo1fyQk7yh3Os8iI_ooA-VAOXsm-VOKXPFieZQDM19CzUZrq8wITXXxvCklukYjdPc8PKUPnf-c7eXUbwAAAP__XyeDGA). Keepers and veterinarians cared for the beloved hippo around the clock. body:
Join us for a listening session!
| | | |
# Dear Peter,

Governor-elect Helena Buonanno Foulkes and her transition team invite you to a community listening session.
These sessions are a chance for Rhode Islanders to share their ideas for the new administration: what should happen in the first 100 days, the first six months, the first year, and the first term. Everything shared will go to the transition team. You are welcome to join whichever session works best for you.
All sessions will be held from 5:00 PM to 7:00 PM.

* Providence: Tuesday, November 24, Elmwood Community Center, 75 Atlantic Ave

* Aquidneck Island: Monday, November 30, CCRI Newport County Campus, 1 John H. Chafee Blvd, Newport

* Warwick: Tuesday, December 1, Warwick Central Library, 600 Sandy Lane

* Woonsocket: Wednesday, December 2, Woonsocket Education Center, 115 Main St

## Trump, Putin, Xi Meet at Historic Summit
President Trump sat down with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China, yesterday for the [first-ever three-way meeting](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OpDAQhJ_GZEZum-EncHAJ2Vx6ITKmPfTJNsg0w-7br5hX2KSSkr5Sff-e09NRpPz66xJaDtuU8ToiMmOZ_ErZHWdKxD66c8GjoN_KQpNWupUAUqvJeaY3TlAtNiBqNBVa6IYHdI1p-mq1CsEFHxx0be9U1_cGB6Na1ajHDCE0FdkbB6AVgNG6q433w9DP3gVs5yF40ShciLdS_98o84ohfm9vLLXfUhXtyrwfwvwRehR6vK6r9nn2dyn0eKOFHgHuGIQeuZxpl18k95MpSy4UHWNxUSZEpvySn9v1yilWxS77RTHS0XaiUa_kKH5W-Xeu3lb_BAAA__9JxX4M) between the leaders of the three nations. ## Islam Set to Pass Christianity by 2035, Pew Says
Muslims will outnumber Christians worldwide by 2035 and become the planet’s largest religious group, according to projections released by the Pew Research Center. [See the report here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOozAQhJ_GdEb2QgIULq6hy7VXIsesYSOD0bLEurc_JdI9wd9MM6OZ0ffnMT08JdqX335DJzFPO5YzoQjyFFba_XltG0lI_prxZAyZZ5rAwF1bq8FMPgi9cbLV7CIiYFOhs91ws13btH21Out9bNtobxAsRoC-jUMwfW_CgGaYsSL3qbMWjLUNQFc3IQxD_ww-4v05xKBagzNJ5vqVaZcVY_qb38h1yFuV3CpynKr5pWBUMJZS6gML44mew1pnXhSMjIkWyruC8TOmYLT2I72CUVbU8ZKLUeeoS-Y06__5Ux_5uJIXyrteOBdZ9cH5hUG-LhgwGkxnFIwVu_kolBKd9061Ztk8pe9H-RnZt4N_AQAA__8GJI5C). The shift is driven by birth rates and age. [Muslim women average 3.1 children](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL3O2yAUQJ8Gb0Rw8U8yeEhVeaj0denwjRaGi7kRGAtwrLx95b5C5yMd6Zzvr_lLU6Bt_a0jjtWlecOzBKwV82w8bbocMVI1QR8WS0aTsqUZBPRcSg5i1qbSG2fZ2NEhAqoGRzk8Ojm0qr03fsSl7dz97kBgL4UbdGe1WlwH_eKE0NDQeOmkBCGlAhhuypjH474Y7bBfHs6wVqClmvLtlWirHl34pDfmm0mxCaOvdS9MPRlMDKbzPG-xbBdjMOHGj8JguqoYTKl6zAymeJRAsfA9UUHLa-LpqNsRF8zc-Eylkt4KX0NadAgfvnw4CNVxHclyizGtWe-eDC-eXL3MOvPnE_wv8fpmakqGLFM_f1xj8Sx_MO9NHu1-UghU-oG1Yo2awr-C-n_f3yP8DQAA___Ir5rM), compared with 2.5 for Christians, and Muslim populations are younger on average. Pew counted 2.27 billion Christians and 2.02 billion Muslims in 2020 and projects 2.57 billion Muslims and 2.52 billion Christians by 2035. Both faiths keep growing. The global Muslim population is projected to [rise 80%](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDvO4yAURleDOyIeflFQTOMu00SjKS0M1_aNwERwHSu7H2W28Nef9Omc8_c-3x1GPLbfLoGlNc8HXDUCEZTZ73i4eqaE5KM7A9QCPpeAsxKq51JyJWbnCd8wyybYFUCBbsDKwXRyaHU7Nrt1PiwgW2nWQTo9dKNZnO5N13di6c0oG7TfOymVkFIrNdy098aMi3cr9ItZPWsFBKRcbs-MB-2wxk9-Q7n5nJpod6JXZfoXUxNTk1v8V-G7MTX9eTA1XVjgQbl8mJrSWSOmyl8lP8ETBJ5POs60QOF-L1gJ3VG5ErrjVy4xVB5d2aASLxBxw3xwqUfVCSGGptjwujBGrP3AWrElh_E_Ff2s5duqfwEAAP__4LmKjA) by 2070 and Christians 30%, with more than half of the world’s Christians living in sub-Saharan Africa by then. In the United States, Christians remain the clear majority, but their share is projected to [fall below half](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykULuO3DAQ-xq580Iaya9CRRp3lzalMSuP7TnI0kKaW-P-PnCAfMFVBAGSIPnnY_lAjpz233iSly0via4aSYTKEg5OWL_OkyVE_FqpFgq5rLyAhr41pgW9YBB-02Ka1W9EQLYhb4apM4OzbmwOHwLqvkdEcjh1qzVu1L2BsbNmDNrZhv0dZwxoYyzA8LAhTNP4DLhR_5y2oJymlSWXx2fmJAdt8Tu_qTxCPpvoD5FXVfaXglnBfF3XIz3DhfXgtEtOt0rBfO-6AYVzwthyEir_mYKZa8SzDUfhKoyJ5buNWHaq0haKvHNO7avkTwq3pbagbadgdmbstJsUzE3x6-viGLn2g3J6P5Hjv4rys2PfHv4GAAD__4PJj4Y) by 2070. ## Diamond Heist Killer Executed
Texas [executed Reinaldo Dennes](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2ypCAUhVeDGV3cC_4QEExi9iad0AK8tkwjWIhtv91P-bYw4alTdX6-P1_Tlw0xpOdvu5GpnyVPia4jUq1UJp9L-k4uZv86_p7zk_bgX_vp4oQCOw7AUUzW1_CmCZrZODFraMhAr1voOyGxWY3sWxIdKKu0h06jUwtKpS0OVst2aJtg7jQAFIBCSHhIjR5QeWpbUoMUTAmaQ83lUVeq9LHHEr_zm8rD562JZq11P5j8xXBkOF7X9Xit-bxNhqMtNfhIDMf7GMPRl7DdslBINs6Zz5QSHXzN51Fz4j8FnD7kzxpyYjji0HJQg3AeBu6l6LlarOK2dx13SvWeQA8OuqaYeb9CjOHoeqbEc7Mh_mys_4n2bfBfAAAA__8ttotO), 70, Thursday evening in Huntsville for the 1996 murder of Houston jeweler Janos Szucs during a heist of roughly $3.6 million in diamonds that were never recovered. A retired prosecutor called it "[kind of an inside job](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDuu6yAURUeDOyLOwZ9QULzGXV57SwvDcUyCwQKcz-yvkincemsvLa2fy3QxPvh4_W820vW1pCnSswSqlfJkU47vOIdk7-V2uCvt3t73Yw4TCuw5AEcxGVv9gyZonJ6FU9CQhkF1MPRCYrNqu0ALjpTBbnZWLqQGQ_PQLUMHTsqh8fpDA0ABKISEk1RoAVtLXUftWQrWCnK-pnyqK1V6mbKEd3pQPtm0NUGvte6FyX8MR4ajmS3Iz8Jw3FOpDMfvhxeqnF5kj0o8k48muMQdxUiFr-koNUV-oycFyoWDUj3fjuwoMxxRiE6KMzIcm6zd_vQh-NIPrBXXzfjwFal_7PfQ-BsAAP__Gs-E9Q)," since Dennes and his brother dealt diamonds in Szucs' building. A cleaning worker let them in through a loading dock, and a guard Dennes shot survived to identify him. [Dennes' last appeal](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDuOwyAQQE-DOyIY_KOg2MZdtt3SwjC2STBYQJzk9itH2hNsOZrR05v3cx2v2nkXlm-9oSqvOY4Bn9ljKZhGE1N4h8lHc8-3h11wd-a-PyY_AoOWck6BjdoUd-DIK6smZiWvUPFONrxrmYBqVbxvRdsxAbLlsu9rwVnTWjPP1komOlk5ddI4B8aBMcEvQoLhUBtsGqx7wUjN0LoS06WsWPCl8-zf8cB0MXGrvFpL2TMRXwQGAkPWQYcFffTuwPOCwHD-RGAwyW1IYPiz55LA8AHSTQeasdAJKb7QPApaenf-TENv-ESPiW7nHAO10Xud6Ioulyopuz_PRW47UrNl085_vMo_cx4KfgMAAP__VTuJ7A) argued Houston police hid that a trial witness was a police informant. The Texas Supreme Court dismissed his challenge to the state's lethal injection drug on Nov. 9. His spiritual adviser, a death penalty opponent, the Rev. Jeff Hood, [said Dennes was "very excited"](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL1ygzAQhJ8GOjEnIf4KFWncOW1K5pBORrFAjDgb_PYZ-xXS7-7s9_1cxyuGGNbbNy5k-PRpXOnYIzFTHm3K62udYrL3_ffhbrQFe98eUxwVqFZIKRSMaDk8aZSlMxO4QZZkZDc0smuhVuVswHuPvnegYainGrFFUD0NjZz6pte6DOa9JqUCqQBqWdWDslJpS01Duq-h0EAucMoVz8R04u7jKz0pVzYtZTQz87YX9VehLoW6HMdRvRkOovs7UKjLpyPCuiCToNMGJid8ysIR8ixwFz6mHByKnVhwEpnQzoJOsg8OaRWZbMpOSNVp6Ie-zMZtR4gx7G1XaLgtGOLnDP_T4dOovwAAAP__xaaIAQ) and called Thursday his "release date." He was the ninth and final person Texas executed this year.
## Cornyn Blocks Trump's Texas Judge Pick
Sen. John Cornyn is [blocking President Trump's nominee](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LvOozAQBeCngY5oZszNhYtt0mXbLZEZD8GJwcg4t7dfkf8R_nI00jn6zr_LcLE--PX61y5i8nuKwyqvPUjOkgaOaf2sY4h8328Pd5XN8317jGEgoLZCrAgGy9k_ZcDSmRGcxlIMdrrBrgVF5WyUm0bqoa47Tb3mBmvVOlYt9oBapCu9OdIQCZAAFJ6UJkaqWZpG6l5BUYM4n2M65VmyvO0-hU98SjpxXMpg5py3vVB_CjoXdLbbIThex5Gy5yAFnV1cbXBVTo9lq76Y6hbntfoxVqS5B7YOUXdNh8xqasYRqQdS46SaMhm3vXwIfm-7oobrYn349udfzvY09D8AAP__2sB_9g) for a Dallas-area federal judgeship, saying the pick isn't from Texas and hasn't been properly vetted. Elliot Gaiser, 37, a top Justice Department lawyer from Ohio, can't advance without Cornyn's home-state sign-off. "_I'm just not going to rubber-stamp somebody that the White House drops in who's not from Texas, who has no trial experience_ ," Cornyn [said this week](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2SgzAMBeDTmM6MJX4cChfb0GXbLRljC3BiMGOcQG6_A3uE7VRIevO9n3t31867ZfzWM6l0DKFbaN88pUSxMyEun6X3wTy3x8uOtDrzXF-971BgzQE4ik6b5N7UQWZVL2wDGSmQTQWyFgVmk6putjG1sWVf4KBrI5tBaimN7G0lsIHMqfMbAApAIQrIiwYNYGmoqqi8FYKVgqxLIeZpokSH3gb_CW-KuQlz5tWU0rqx4othy7Dd9z0fwlGejnOBYXuODNvrlD_CtPA_Gbdh0d7yFF_zyi8hv7Rk-ajdRjGLyq67895ttWSlGGft_BWb_tnWW-FvAAAA___cpYFP). Cornyn has [pushed the White House](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2OgzAQxfHTmM7RzNiBULjYhi7bbomMPQRvjI3A-br9iuQIWz_pL_3ez7k_2xBDunzbmU15jrlP_Ngil8Jr7_KaXmmI2V2335u_8BLcdbkNsSegWiJKgt66Eu7cY-XNAL7Fig027RGbGhRVkzl57VRtPdv2NMLQNEjOg0U1ukETURXMXkMkQAJQeFAtOSTt-HhkfVIgNLAPJa-HMnHhp93G-Mp3Xg8uz1U0UynLJtSXoE5QVyaeQoz7Jqib8sy7SFC3cbKFBXU1UQutlh-e_Phkyknu8STfVEFdtRq_PEKMYasboeEy2_DuVuWfV90N_QUAAP__WzR-DQ) for months to nominate Fort Worth lawyer Steve Fahey, a federal prosecutor in North Texas for 18 years. The White House has now asked about Fahey, Cornyn said, adding he doesn't want the seat left empty. Sen. Ted Cruz, whose staff first approached Gaiser, said the block would "effectively give the judicial seat to the Democrats," who take over the Senate Jan. 3. The [Justice Department called it](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAQxvGnsTcs7jChGRi6ZEvXjhbGR0KDwQJsJ29fOX2E7qfT__d9X4er8cHH25eZSdenS0OkvQSqlfJgU46vOIZkH-VnnW60ePtY1jEMyPHEABjywdjqNxqgnfTIpzO0pEGdJagTF9jetRIcrHXS9dgDB8f7URI644wxXAjZen18A0AOyLmATpzRAvaWpKT-Q_Cm5zT5mnJX71TpaYoLr7RR7mya26DvtS6lEZ8NXhq87PveHYad6HEcNHhxa34xU1imI95bE1mhaGrK7A_Hal7npTCbYqG8mUPE3mIW0-yjqT5FBqiEVEq2WU_L7kPw5aSant9m48O7pf5zwk3jbwAAAP__zMqIwQ) "political obstruction" of a "highly qualified nominee."
## DHS Warns Texas Over ICE Cooperation
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin [warned Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOgzAQRL8GOpB3wYALF9fQ5dorkbE34MuCkTEh-fsT-YXrnjTS08z83Iab8ezX6dsspNPrHoaVzp0pJYqDDXF9ryMH-9h_DzfR5u1jO0YeUGBTABQoBmOTf9IAudOjcApy0tAqCW0jKsxnrSx1tXCiGSVKaI1VCABY0V1Q3UmVe33ZAFAAClFBWSm0gLUlKanuKpHVgpxPIZZppkQvs9_5HZ4USxuWnPWc0rZn1VeGfYb9eZ7l28whXGmG_bUnw34L7JO3F5qYvGW6cDmY_VqcJq578VEXNhzsio3NdJAroJFYq05BOaeF86jddnpmvzdtVotpMZ4_LdI_z3tq_AsAAP__6VWEIA) and other Texas leaders Wednesday that scaling back ICE cooperation would be "one of the worst derelictions of duty we've seen in a very long time." Hinojosa, a Democrat taking office in January, has said ICE is "[making us less safe](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unDAQhZ_GdF6Nh_-CIo27mzYlMvawOGswsofl8vYRq-QJ0ow0mqNv9J1fX-OX8cFvz59mpYG_5zhudOZAzJRGG9N2bVOI9pV_H-5Ju7ev_ZjCiICNVEoijMayf9OoCjdM4HpV0KDavlZtAyUWy6AqVzfGQlk3MM9Q1V3f9j0BVt00k3WFH26aUggKAUr1KHu0CitLdU1VV4KogJznmB68ENO3yXO44pvSw8a1CMPCvGdR_hCoBerzPB9HNhydue6AQJ05pkugvtU-q2ESqD8ogfp-L1ArdY_-30EGv3qW3pK0Me6UDPu4ycnYVzB5kW7JktOx7tK41W8-89_EEo_McROoe-zqroQSoBWoizS4_fQh-Ny0ooLnanz4KPB_Nv8e8E8AAAD___EYl80)." Houston Mayor John Whitmire, also a Democrat, told police to stop alerting ICE during traffic stops, contacting the agency only once someone is jailed. Still, Hinojosa said she and President Trump want the same thing at the border [after a positive phone call](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2O4zAMhU8jdwpEyr-Fi23UzbZbGrLExJooliHR8fj2C-cK0xAg8OEj3_v3NX3ZEMP6-GtfNPLPPU0rHSUSM-XJpbye6xyTe5bv3T9oC-657XOcUGErASSqyToOb5qg8uOs_AAVjdANDXSt0lgto-tq0kT9fW6xti3YZobaabg3gL1uqArjZQNABaiUhpse0AHWjpqG6l4rUSvygVO-8UJMP7bc45nelG8uvao4LsxbEfqPQCPQHMdx24vl5O15AQJN4ZRPgeaK9lktk0DzUQk013mBBuAag0DzCKuVS1jTdypWso3PIj-wnFP2lOVhY5SF3J4Dn_IIvEifVhu95Ly_NoFmwL5VoHulOoGmyqPfjhBjKG0navV42RA_3_MvS3-P-D8AAP__8NOVpA) between them. She suggested technology instead of a physical wall and raised concerns about one in Big Bend National Park. State law requires sheriffs who run jails to [sign agreements with ICE](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAQhZ8Gd0Qw4L_CxTbu7rZbWgMMCRtiIpjYN2-_yr7CLY-OdHS-78_X9oUpp_36Gx-08Hcs205ny8RMdfOl7u_d5eLv7e8rXOmZ_P35cnkDBYPUWoLa0HM6aNNdWJwKs-5o0ePc63FQBrrbouYJfO_jaN3orNLzHNQ0xklRP4fgqEvLZ01rUBqUMvpiZvAarKe-JzsZJayikLjUC9-I6RtbzO9yUL348ujycmN-NmF-CVgFrOd5Xu7Hiz6lgBUrJ59JwPoBE7Dm4jELWLnikZr05bXzW7Yb1RRjkyXG5EnitRI9aGf5SY2RSWY8BawwzNJMZozagqTejdKCQ4mDC1J5JEJLpjfY1SU8z5RzasMorLo-MOX_j_mHoo8F_gUAAP__r0eR_w) by Dec. 1. Travis County's sheriff picked the most limited option, one jail officer serving ICE warrants, but said signing "does not mean I agree with the law."

Derek, on Wednesday, a Trump-appointed U.S. attorney threatened Adam with “significant legal consequences” — all for demanding answers the American people deserve. Trump’s DOJ is coming after Adam for asking the questions the American people have every right to have answered — _because this administration’s corruption has driven up costs for every American family._ This isn’t the first time Trump’s cronies have threatened Adam for conducting oversight, and it won’t be the last. He’s not backing down, but he needs to know his grassroots team has his back. **[Rush a donation to Adam’s campaign right now, and then read his response below.](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/8046?t=11&amount=10&refcode=aschiff_email_112026_attorneyrrbump&akid=10949%2E5257348%2Ey2diSE)** | | [DONATE→](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/8046?t=15&amount=10&refcode=aschiff_email_112026_attorneyrrbump&akid=10949%2E5257348%2Ey2diSE)

From: **Adam Schiff** <[reply@e.adamschiff.com](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/62?t=7&refcode=aschiff_email_112026_attorneyrrbump&akid=10949%2E5257348%2Ey2diSE)>

Derek, this morning a Trump-appointed U.S. attorney sent me a letter on Justice Department letterhead, and it reads just like a threat.
_It is meant that way, too._
Aaron Reitz is a MAGA loyalist who promised to investigate the people investigating Trump, and today he made good on it — citing federal criminal statutes, demanding I preserve my records, and warning of “significant legal consequences” if I don’t.
**[Attacks like this will not deter me from investigating corruption in the Trump Administration. Will you chip in $10 to show you have my back and keep me in the Senate?](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/8046?t=16&amount=10&refcode=aschiff_email_112026_attorneyrrbump&akid=10949%2E5257348%2Ey2diSE)**

In addition to sending this tweet, here is everything I did to earn this menacing letter from the Department of Justice:
I demanded to know who paid for Trump’s $900 million ballroom. Who funded Freedom 250. What’s really behind the ABC and CBS settlements, and the pro bono deal Kirkland & Ellis cut with the White House.
These are the questions any oversight committee would ask, and the questions the American people have every right to have answered. Because this administration’s corruption has driven up costs for every American family.
DOJ’s letter calls these donors “private Americans,” but a billionaire who writes a check to the president is not simply a private citizen minding his own business.
And one more thing this Trump enabler at DOJ didn’t like. He didn’t like my calling him “bat shit crazy.” But no self-respecting, rule of law abiding prosecutor would put their name on such meritless drivel.
Reitz already sent the same letter to Senator Blumenthal, to Senator Warren, and to Senator Slotkin, and the message to the rest of Senate Democrats is unmistakable: the Justice Department exists to protect the people paying Trump — and asking where the money came from will be treated as a criminal act.
I won’t back down. I won’t be intimidated.
Millions of Americans rejected this corruption at the ballot box two weeks ago. They gave us the majority to ask hard questions and follow the money until we find out who is buying access to our government and what those individuals are getting in return.
**That’s why I need you to have my back right now.**

body:

# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20261120-1&t=1&akid=4257%2E587540%2ES36GFA)
Peter,
Have you ever wondered why Congress is so old? Why Representatives in their 80s are in leadership roles instead of passing the torch? Just look at Democrats’ rules (or lack thereof) for committee chairs:
Unlike the Republican Caucus, the Democratic Caucus has no rules limiting how long a Member can serve as the head of a committee.
This may seem like inside baseball, but this little-known internal rule is what keeps Congress older, and prevents young, dynamic leaders from rising through the ranks in the U.S. House.
**But this historic new class is fighting back:**
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261120_1_term.fstzaD&refcode=em20261120-4257&amount=5&t=2&akid=4257%2E587540%2ES36GFA)
That’s right: _We could see term limits for Democratic congressional committees for the first time._
This rule change would encourage more members of Congress to retire, creating more open seats for the next generation of leaders. It would also create a culture of competition where ideas and competency are what gets someone elected to chair a committee, instead of seniority.
Just look at what Congressman Robert Garcia was able to do as the Democratic head of the Oversight Committee with the Epstein files. His work played a significant role in exposing the rot and corruption of the Trump administration that became a dominating theme of this election cycle. Imagine if we had that kind of energy and foresight on _every committee._
It’s no surprise that this move is being driven by younger, newer leaders. They know they were elected to upend the status quo and get things done. And they shouldn’t be hamstrung by establishment politicians desperate to hold onto power.
**[Peter, our work didn’t stop on Election Day. That’s why we need you with us. David Hogg

## Judge Holds ICE in Contempt
A federal judge in Denver [held ICE officials in contempt](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkL-OrCAUxp8GOwygwlhQ3MZubntLczwcZriLYoAZ49tv3GSzD7DdL_mS79-_-3yHEMP2-Asr2Yp-3ugokWqlPJcdkADB0XpCyHvK1afkYJuVUJpLyZWYAWt409xD46z3CkE3ZKUZB2lG3Y3N0_qbXkgvhgzcaMQBSBo14CJ7Z0Qvb02wl5-USshOiE63fpC-GxYkp7TsYGC9IBdqym19EqaYMrjk45nelFtMaxPts9a9sO4PUxNT03Ec7bbgteXSmZouZGp6Ff5D_1_uQbzAWXhA4is44mvCD8onx_TKlafsKBf-HckzbqClkNo02br9CDGGog3rxWOFEL-61F_e-LbqMwAA___ukImI) Wednesday for re-arresting a man moments after she ordered him released, writing that the practice "made a mockery of court orders." The case involved Ramon Quintero Alvarez, an immigrant whom ICE re-detained under a [direct order from agency leaders](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAQhJ_GdETeNZhQuPgbuvztlWhjrxOfDEZmL1He_kSkPME1U32aTzNfl_lCKaf19p8WduLjvPJzzyzCdd438kyeAi8vSnUrVWIpgdYZNdoWoEU9k5f04LmjJrgY0ZNt2MEw9jCM1ozN3WnTUbQxDtaD6cerHg1x1HDWZzIx9E1yRx8AajBaG3uKPUTTXz0HtGCoV53mkKTUk9zZl1wqhRLzqzy4nnxZmuzuItuuzD-Fk8Lpw7zHpJUPSOF0aBROAEeMCqfvn3Dj9kO3yXOb1taXVXjZROHUVBe2Z8o57XZQnb4tlPJbKX986-HwNwAA__-OX35U). Filings point to at least 18 similar Colorado cases. In a [15-page ruling](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkDGP3CAUhH8N7lgBNlguKNK4u7QprXe8h02EwXpwu9p_HzlSpPTXTDOfZkbz62P7gJRT2X_CSb6HuBV6tUy9E2_tgkAQAOl8Q-Krco-1IpTNKOOk1tKoDUJPT9omGNDHaAK4gbyeF6vnxY3LcHgE-2lHpUktiNqAnSnM0Sqn4mTcjEPyd57WRulRqdE9otVxtJ-B0Dg9ghWTIky98qMfFGquDFhjftcn8SPUc8j-6P1qYvwhzCrM-o9pX-X2hVnvBmFWrW9Z_kPk7y_cSR41Y5MpkExFhlo6nVeXsbJkAmZqPZVdpvNMO0PpTVZGYkIZmQiFWQf2eL1Szqm5WUxqPyHlv-P6N399evMnAAD__wJ7jng), Federal Judge Charlotte Sweeney excoriated top Colorado ICE and Homeland Security officials. She signaled she would not hesitate to reopen the matter if more violations occur. Sweeney declined to impose further penalties after officials confirmed under oath that the practice had stopped. ICE and Homeland Security did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
## Feds to Investigate Thompson School District
The U.S. Department of Education is [investigating Thompson School District](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO5CAQRL8GZ4ygPTbrgOASZ3vphVYPNOOWMFjQO6v5-5NPui_YpJIqVZXen8_tEzlzef7Gg7yEtBX67plEqG39xEAYMNLxRm5nbZJqjVg2MDBrazWYDYPwi7Y7DtGnBAHngbx1y2TdMo_LsPv4cQdyy-Qmio6MdRAcPPAxxQVsojSwv_qsBWNHY8b5liabxukRKMJsR5zU3VBkqe0mO4Waa8NYU37XF7VbqMeQ_S5ydjX-UrAqWP9n-le5fAXrtaBgtfaSDwWr7PU4ey26h73WrCN3aRxEJ4rUMGsuL-rCTxSuRUvD0p9UIjV91syBqWtpX8epYB2aj-c358x9dupungdy_ndMfsj05eFvAAAA__-IKY4f) in Loveland, alleging its policies conceal information from parents about a child's gender identity. Federal officials cited [forms like Gender Support Plans](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu4yAQRb8Gd0RmsElSUGzj7m27pTWBIUbCgGCerff3K6-UL9h2Rvfo3vPna_3CmGJ-_8adLLuwZjp7ImZqa6_oCB162n8wtloah1I85hVGMFIpCeOKjuNB64SDtyGAQzOQVffnrO5Po5_DZsHfNfgZjCJNfsIA5NE8ptfDmAfoxxDtxVMKRqXHUZtbmFXQ88uRB6M0zmIayUcu7cYbuZJKQ19C-ikHtZsr-5Dsxly70L8ELAKW8zxv7tWvLddfwPJJCViuq4DFU8XGO2WW5L8dcixZxnxQ5_hGpi47uUYs35Q9Ndm_62VA1oS5yw9P8lb22kuW3W2lJOlj5xYdC1iGZn09Y0qxm7uYxveOMf3ry_-p-rDwNwAA__9l95kJ), which ask students about names, pronouns, and whether the school should keep their gender identity hidden from parents. Thompson was one of [five districts named Nov. 18](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OpDAQRk9jMrf8zxAQbEI2m26ICrvclGQwsmsaze1XvcFeYNLvSZ_03p_P9ROo0Pn8DQfOHPN64t0LMmNb-wURIULC4xuoXbVxrjXBuRplgtRaGrVCZHrh6mBIc84mQhhw1uPk9TgFOw377Dc9Re3G9OGUH0cDaH1Q4D42SN6nNND8_tPaKG2VsuGRvc7WbxGTCdqCF05hIq7twTvGWmqDVHP5ri9sj1iPocw789WF_SXMIsxy3_djepu8qTALNKZYUJjlPQqzYPqKwFRPYZavLhNe0PjAk2XN8j-UdL6wMz2B6XxK3utx9XrKHvdai0zUuVFkYZbRShddQlAgMbsknQMtYQybRGv9Nk0RNYShzem6qRTqYRROPQ-g8s-Afxj_NZu_AQAA___aU5q_) in the latest round of investigations, alongside districts in Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Illinois, and Minnesota. The district, which serves more than 15,000 students across 31 schools, said it received the information Wednesday and is working to evaluate it and determine next steps.
## Colorado Vies to Host Space Academy
Colorado has [submitted its bid](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OszAQAJ8GOiP_gAmFi69Jl6-9Ei32GiwZL7Idorz9KSdFl_7aGe1od79u8w1CDGn9Dzuaav2c8FEi1op5LgdYBAsO9yeEfFCunshBmiWXmgnBJJ_B1nDi3EPrjPfSgm7RiHEaxDhpNbWbuVjP1XTRMPVjPyi44Ogsd4tSIxdcL20wr54QkgvFudKdH4RXw2LRSS0UDE3P0YVKuasbWoqUwZGPTzoxd5b2Npqt1qM06l8jr428ri-TKBfyPljs3jPdSueHbuT1de4HYQfFUBgkx2JlvzSHHU7MwCAluieL7J0srNyXPZQSKLGNSmX3FCo6VipULG027niEGEPRY9PzdYcQf3auf3z3aeR3AAAA___84JsO) to host the future U.S. Space Academy, proposing a 508-acre site in the Banning Lewis Ranch area of Colorado Springs. President Trump signed an [executive order in August](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkL2K6zAQRp9G7mT0Y8txoeJyF3dJsc2WZjIaJQLZMpISb95-cdg32G5g4HDO93WezxBiWG8XWMhW9PNKe4lUK-W5bIAECI6WF4S8pVx9Sg7WWQlluJRciRmwhifNHTTOeq8QTENWDmMvh9HosbnboRsGQ6M4jfqKp35E6fUAhLLTUqlON8EePCmVkFoIbVrfS6_7K5JTRmroWSfIhZpyW--EKaYMLvn4Sk_KLaalifZe61aY_sfUxNS073uL13K0HH-mpuNkaqr5sWy8hNtaOH0TPg55nrKjzGvimAkqceCPwt_1_Df_wOoprBWDY_rj_-WTC8WFUbrJ1m17iDEUM7BO3BYI8S1V_7jn06qfAAAA__9BfIpU) to begin creating the academy for the U.S. Space Force, NASA, and the civilian spaceflight industry. Under the proposal, [UCCS could house 300 students](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLGupCAYhZ8GOwz8Kq4FxTZ2s-2W5hd-RjIoBlAzb79xsjf3AW5zinOSLyff38f0QB_89vyDK-li3LTRlQOVQmnKOxpCg5bWN_q0x1RcjBa3CQQoLiUHMaEp_qSpxcpq58CgqkjLfuhkP6hmqBbdtgq7TqL9RaoTg3OibwekGZySs0NTeX3zpAQhGyEaVbtOuqabDVlQssGOtYKsLzHVZSETQ0xoowvveFKqTVyroJdS9sya3wxGBuN1XfXrVc57ZDDeeAajlHf0DMYvBs_HvPqS-ewt_y735Ldn5ks8MnF3lCMRPzL_-OD_hTAYq6TtfvkQfFY9a8VzRR8-f8oPVZ4a_gUAAP__EyeJxg) starting in 2028, though the academy itself would not welcome students until 2031 at the earliest. Colorado faces competition from the [24 other states](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO8yAQBOCnsTssWGyIC4q_SZe_vdLawBKjw8GCTay8_SnRvcH1oxl983VZLphyut_-40aOfVzudLRMzFSXtqMn9Bhoe2Gqe6kcSwl4X0CCEUoJkAt6Tk9aRuyDixE8mp6csvOk7Gz03K9uBIqS0MwQ7UlaKyNomJWBYOGqouyTe_cpBVJpKbUZ4qSinq6eAhilcepGSSFxqQOv5EsuFUOJ-VWeVAdftj67lXlvnf7XwbmD83EcwxtyEH2_Ax2cGyNTE75sOzEJLmItjQXXx7Y38WjioxW_XKHAgp1Oqq8u7EfKOTVju1HeNkz5s8l_vOvp4CcAAP__qrOAFA) that submitted proposals, and a presidential commission is due to send its recommendations to Trump by Dec. 26.

## Maricopa Certifies Faster Count
Maricopa County supervisors certified the Nov. 3 general election results after the county reported final tallies in eight days, its [fastest pace](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkL1u6zAMRp9G3hTox7GjQcNdvOWuHQ1GphKismVIjIPk6Yu47RN0PgTxnfNxHs9AiZbrf5jRM7ziuOCjJmTGMkaojGXLjCHfF47pHqBiLTQaZTqptTRqhMC04dhCM3nbBde3DXrdu6PunbNtc_NodW_1CZS7oAIVW9P1YMDGLihs1dSQf__T2iht1dHaAwAYF0_olIuXUziKVuFEnMuBbwiFXnmBmJ55w3IIeW6SvzGvVdh_wgzCDJ8MOxBm-LmWa07EFKp8-wkzYMLAlBdhhhkKhbyC3C2f8hfJgvWeuMq9Q-VvLgMsG9TaFD-tD0qJateLVl1noLSv4b-G3Lz5CgAA__9aDIzs) since at least 2006. Recorder Justin Heap [skipped the canvass](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkL1ugzAURp_GbEb-IYAHD13Y0rUjujHXiVuDkX0BhaevGilP0Af4js53vq7jFUIMy_0TZrQEpx8XPEpEIsyjh0KY90To0raQj5uDgiWHUQnVcim5EiM4CjuODVST1a0zXVOhlZ25yM4Y3VQPO8l2mhBcL4TpTNs5D7rT4PseNZimqYL940mphNTionUNAMr4Ho0w_ta7C2sEToFSrumBkMOZFvDxmXbMtUtzFe2DaC1MfzA1MDUcx1H_fJ9nnfKdqQEjOgppKUwNb3PZMzXMkINLK_DXvye_JcgTT56XbcW8h5Jy4Q4zBR-w8Nf2DeMZyxapVNlO6xFiDKXtWCPuM4T4sqL_Bt2t-g0AAP__ihmNaQ) and held a separate briefing, touting changes his office made in signature verification. | Hey Peter,
Yesterday, House Democrats held a closed-door vote to choose our nominee for Speaker. You may have already heard how I voted, but I wanted you to hear directly from me about why I made that decision.
I joined six of my fellow incoming members in a statement explaining that our constituents sent us to Congress with a mandate, and that our conversations with leadership aren't finished.
Much of that mandate came from you over the last several weeks.
After our virtual town hall on Sunday, hundreds of you filled out our survey and sent us messages, and you made your voices clear. You want Medicare for All, money out of our elections, and an end to sending American weapons to Israel to fuel the genocide against Palestinians. You also wrote to me about student debt, Social Security, and your kids' schools. And again and again, you came back to the same frustration. We know what working people need, but the billionaires and corporations bankrolling Washington keep standing in the way.
That's why I voted against electing Hakeem Jeffries to be the caucus nominee for Speaker of the House because I promised to fight for an agenda that the working people of Denver deserve.
While this week was the first preliminary vote, the final vote isn't until January. And we still have time to work with leadership to prove that our party is finally ready to fight for the people who put us here. Until then, I'll keep pushing for the agenda you elected me to deliver. I'm not backing down, and I'm certainly not giving up.
Keep your messages coming. We're listening, and we're bringing your demands straight into the halls of Congress.
- Melat

subject: Let me explain?
body:
Peter, let me
explain my dilemma.

Trump and his team have talked about having DHS go after me for months,
and now they’ve made it official.

DHS agents showed up at my doorstep and raided my home. Now we’ve gone

investigation is entirely a partisan delusion.

# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=241186%2E444211%2EmKcBSn)
Powered by People does the work that works, and we do it all year long. Many political organizations start organizing a few months before Election Day and hope for the best. They set up shop over the summer and knock doors through the fall. Then on November 4th, they pack up and disappear until the next cycle.
**We take a personal, year-round approach, and we know it pays off.**
Our volunteers build real relationships over months and years to register and turn out the Texans others overlook. So when Election Day is around the corner, that voter already has a real person to call with questions about how to vote, where their polling place is, or what to bring.
That’s the difference between a voter who intends to vote and one who actually shows up.
To build those long-lasting, personal relationships, we organize year-round. Just last week, our volunteers were at Texas Southern University in Houston registering students to vote:
It would be easy to sit back and relax after the incredible victories earlier this month. But we refuse to.
**Every single voter we connect with now will make a difference in 2028 and beyond.**
Year-round organizing takes year-round resources. Most donors stop giving once the election is over, and that’s exactly when we need support most, so we can keep our volunteers on campuses and in communities all over Texas.
[**Will you chip in $3 to keep Powered by People organizing all year long?**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20261120.88NEHn&refcode=ema20261120-241186&t=3&akid=241186%2E444211%2EmKcBSn)
Whether you can donate today or not, thank you for being a part of PxP.
—Aimee

There was Governor Gavin Newsom on Sunday, standing on Ukrainian soil in Lviv, announcing what his press office styled "new lifesaving aid for the defenders of freedom." The manifest is genuinely impressive: a 50-bed field medical station, more than 1,300 hospital beds, more than 11 million bandages, thousands of wound-care kits, protective equipment, oxygen concentrators, wheelchairs, and portable generators. Ukraine's wounded deserve the best we can send them. Nobody in California looks at a bandage and resents a Ukrainian soldier for needing it.
But notice the word doing the heavy lifting in the coverage -- the Sacramento Bee's word, lifted straight from the administration's framing: "**surplus**." California donated its _surplus_ supplies. Surplus is a term of art. It means the state has inventoried its own needs, run the math on the next earthquake, the next firestorm, the next flood, and certified that it can spare this particular field hospital, these particular beds, these eleven million bandages. So the obvious question, the one no one on the trip seems to have asked before the cameras rolled: _who ran that math_ , and may we see it?
Because California has run this experiment before, and the results are gathering dust in state warehouses. In 2006, spooked by avian flu, California built one of the most ambitious emergency medical stockpiles in the country -- more than 50 million N95 respirators at its height, a ventilator reserve, and three 200-bed mobile field hospitals parked and ready for the Big One. Then the funding lapsed. Successive administrations, Republican and Democratic alike, let the supplies expire and the mobile hospitals drift out of the fleet. By March 2020, when COVID arrived, the state's famous cache of 21 million face masks was so old that age itself disqualified much of it, and California was begging in the same panicked global market as everyone else, discovering that a mask that cost pennies in 2019 cost $3.30 by April -- if you could find one at all...

body:
On October 28, GIFFORDS Law Center filed an amicus brief ahead of those oral arguments, urging the Supreme Court to uphold assault weapons bans in Connecticut and Cook County, Illinois.
#

Team --
On December 2nd, the Supreme Court will hear oral arguments on _Viramontes v. Cook County_ and _Grant v. Higgins._
The Court’s ruling will decide whether assault weapons can be banned.
On October 28th, GIFFORDS Law Center filed an amicus brief ahead of those oral arguments, urging the Supreme Court to uphold assault weapons bans in Connecticut and Cook County, Illinois.
But what we are talking about in this case is not simply the banning of assault weapons. It is whether communities can come together, elect representatives, and pass measures that will protect their citizens. That’s democracy itself.
GIFFORDS Law Center takes on the gun lobby in courts across the nation. And with these cases before the Supreme Court and decisions expected next year, the role GIFFORDS plays in the fight against gun violence has never been more important.
We’ve made significant progress, and your support has been an essential part of that.
[**Now, we’re asking you to make a donation so that work can continue. Please, chip in to GIFFORDS PAC before these oral arguments at the Supreme Court.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q42026.PjNIJI&refcode=em261120-1-b&t=1&akid=12091%2E3935704%2EmLltUZ)

Now that voters have delivered an absolute mandate and handed Democrats the majority, **_Attorney General Todd Blanche is trying to use the full power of the Justice Department to threaten our committee and block us from investigating the Trump administration._**
We know why: _They are terrified of what we’re going to find._
They spent years acting like they were above the law—profiteering off the presidency, abusing power, and hiding the truth. Now that I am stepping into the Chairman’s seat on the House Oversight Committee, they are panicking because they know their free ride is over.
If Todd Blanche thinks he can threaten members of Congress to protect Donald Trump and his cronies from lawful, constitutional oversight, **he picked the wrong fight.**
We are opening the books. We are exposing the corruption. And no threat from the Department of Justice is going to stop us.

body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Senator Chuck Schumer and Rep. Hakeem Jeffries want you to think they were
responsible for the blue tsunami we saw this Election Day and that those
wins are proof that they deserve to lead the House and Senate.

But they weren’t the ones who made those wins possible.

Democrats made historic gains, taking back the U.S. House and Senate,
flipping multiple state legislatures, and winning key gubernatorial races
in states all over the country, including Southern states that Democratic
leaders said were long shots.

We did that in spite of Schumer and Jeffries, not because of them.

Just look at Mississippi, where Democrat Scott Colom beat GOP incumbent
Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith with little to no help from Schumer and the DSCC.

So many of these midterm races were won because of years of dedicated
organizing paired with principled candidates who built campaigns based on
the issues impacting everyday people.

Working-class families and individuals across party lines are sick and
tired of the status quo that serves corporate interests, billionaires, and
lobby groups like AIPAC — the Democrats who acknowledged this and
committed to change saw a surge of grassroots support.

Voters made clear they want progressive leaders who will fight for things
like Medicare for All and an end to unconditional military aid to Israel
and who have the courage to challenge the status quo in Congress. They
want leaders who will stand up to their own party when it means fighting
for what they believe in.

That's exactly why we're so proud of the newly elected Justice Democrats.
Every single one voted against Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker, making clear
that they won't simply fall in line or hand party leadership their support
without a fight.

They understand that winning elections is only the beginning. Now comes
the work of delivering on the agenda voters sent them to Congress to fight
for.

| Letter from the Chair...
---
| A Thanksgiving Message
As an optimist by nature and by choice, I give thanks for all the graces, benefits, and blessings I have received. I acknowledge that they come through no merit of my own, but solely from the kindness of God's mercy.
One benefit of growing older is the ability to look back and see God's hand at work. We all face trials, and I give thanks for those as well. In many ways I am even more grateful for the hard seasons, for it is through them that I have learned the most and taken far less for granted.
From the times I suffered abuse, I am thankful that I learned compassion for others who are hurting. I have come to understand that none of us can end all suffering, yet we can pause and help those God places in our path.
From the seasons when I lacked money to meet bills, I learned that hard times pass and that I can be content with what I have.
From the moments I was ashamed or humiliated--sometimes justly, sometimes not--I am thankful that I learned to be more careful in judging others and their motives. None of us fully knows the burdens and quiet pain others carry.
From lost or fractured relationships, I am thankful for the friends and family with whom the bonds remain intact. I value them even more, knowing that nothing is permanent or guaranteed.
From the odd illnesses and the months of chronic fatigue, I am thankful for every day of good health. I also pray for those I know who are currently suffering and facing the challenges poor health brings.
From the disappointment of this year's lost elections, I am grateful for the candidates who ran and did win. While not complacent about the losses, I recognize that the outcome could have been far worse.
And every day, I remain thankful for the country into which I was graced to be born, the state of Nebraska I choose to call my home, my family and friends, and the unfailing grace of God.
Forward.
Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

From the moments I was ashamed or humiliated--sometimes justly, sometimes not--I am thankful that I learned to be more careful in judging others and their motives. None of us fully knows the burdens and quiet pain others carry. From lost or fractured relationships, I am thankful for the friends and family with whom the bonds remain intact. I value them even more, knowing that nothing is permanent or guaranteed. From the odd illnesses and the months of chronic fatigue, I am thankful for every day of good health. I also pray for those I know who are currently suffering and facing the challenges poor health brings. From the disappointment of this year's lost elections, I am grateful for the candidates who ran and did win. While not complacent about the losses, I recognize that the outcome could have been far worse. And every day, I remain thankful for the country into which I was graced to be born, the state of Nebraska I choose to call my home, my family and friends, and the unfailing grace of God. Forward.
