clean_body: | Big news, friend! My Democratic colleagues in the House have elected me to serve as our Battleground Leadership Representative for the next Congress! Here’s what this role means: Members like me who represent the most competitive districts in the country, ones that can swing either way, get a representative who speaks for all of us directly to House Democratic leadership. Now, when decisions are made about what bills come to the floor, what fights we pick, and how we tell the country what we stand for, I’ll be at the table as the voice for districts like ours. And this year, that’s a lot of districts: more than 70, the largest class of battleground Democrats since this position was created. Those 70+ seats are the reason Democrats have the majority. No battleground districts, no majority. It’s that simple. And keeping that majority means proving to the voters who took a chance on us that they made the right call. Here in mid-Michigan, working families are doing everything right and still feeling the squeeze every month. They want real change that makes their lives better. My job is to bring that message to the leadership table and keep our focus on lowering costs and delivering results people can actually feel. Let’s get to work, Kristen | = | We'd hate to see you go, but you can click here if you'd like to . Thank you for supporting Kristen McDonald Rivet for Congress! Kristen for Michigan P.O. Box 854 Bay City, MI 48707 United States

# **Mamdani unveils plan to close Rikers, delays deadline to 2032**
Mayor Zohran Mamdani **[announced plans to close Rikers Island by 2032,](https://substack.com/redirect/fb0b5648-46a2-48cb-9c5a-aebc507cf9b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** pushing past the original legal deadline requiring replacement jails by 2027, fulfilling a long-held goal despite past criticism from President Trump and opposition from predecessor Eric Adams.
[| | | | | Townhall.com
---
@townhallcom
Socialist NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani says he's closing Rikers Island and replacing it with four borough-based jails starting in 2029 that will "house thousands fewer New Yorkers." Mamdani: "Dignity for everyone means safety for everyone."
| 2:34 PM * Nov 20, 2026 * 4.6K Views18 Replies * 2 Reposts * 8 Likes

* **The plan hinges on reducing the jail 's roughly 6,000-person population** to about 4,500 through diversion programs, supervised early release, expanded housing and social services, and reinstating an online bail payment system, though funding sources remain unclear.
* **Rikers, a 413-acre complex between Queens and the Bronx known by nicknames like "Torture Island,"** has long drawn criticism over conditions; Mamdani called closing it a "legal and moral obligation" toward building a safer, more humane correctional system.

# **Mamdani arrested twice by NYPD unit he is now disbanding**
Mayor Zohran Mamdani's announcement disbanding the NYPD's Strategic Response Group omitted his own history with the unit, which **[zip-tied and arrested him](https://substack.com/redirect/b8c94748-bc21-40d3-970b-fe2f37cda094?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** during protests in 2021 and 2024, before he launched his mayoral campaign.

* **The SRG will be folded into counterterrorism functions,** replaced by two new units -- a 30-officer First Amendment Support Team focused on de-escalation and a Patrol Support Division -- alongside new restrictions banning tactics like kettling, long guns, pepper spray, and tear gas against protesters.
* **Mamdani had publicly pledged to disband the unit back in December 2024** after his own arrest, fulfilling that promise Monday. Police Benevolent Association President Patrick Hendry criticized the move, saying Mamdani is prioritizing his "radical base" over public safety.

# **Latest tech failure hits America 's farmers**
The USDA has experienced multiple system outages since Monday after its Cybersecurity and Privacy Operations Center **[detected a security incident,](https://substack.com/redirect/c58e3827-a233-42c3-86fc-508e0ccf3a9d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** forcing a reset of database passwords and affecting farmer loan and financial aid programs.

---|---|---
* **The disruption adds to a wave of recent tech outages nationwide** affecting banks, airlines, and other systems; Trump has dismissed the idea of a coordinated foreign cyberattack, calling the incidents isolated, even as the administration searches for a new national cyber director.
* **USDA officials gave conflicting explanations,** with one attributing outages to routine software updates while internal guidance warned staff of continued intermittent disruptions. A GAO report released the same week found the USDA has only partially met cybersecurity preparedness recommendations, warning of potential risks to the food supply.

Rikers, a 413-acre complex between Queens and the Bronx known by nicknames like "Torture Island," has long drawn criticism over conditions; Mamdani called closing it a "legal and moral obligation" toward building a safer, more humane correctional system. Mamdani arrested twice by NYPD unit he is now disbanding Mayor Zohran Mamdani's announcement disbanding the NYPD's Strategic Response Group omitted his own history with the unit, which during protests in 2021 and 2024, before he launched his mayoral campaign. The SRG will be folded into counterterrorism functions, replaced by two new units -- a 30-officer First Amendment Support Team focused on de-escalation and a Patrol Support Division -- alongside new restrictions banning tactics like kettling, long guns, pepper spray, and tear gas against protesters. Mamdani had publicly pledged to disband the unit back in December 2024 after his own arrest, fulfilling that promise Monday. Police Benevolent Association President Patrick Hendry criticized the move, saying Mamdani is prioritizing his "radical base" over public safety. Hakeem Jeffries vows to investigate "MAGA extremists," including Musk Incoming House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries told MS Now host Jen Psaki that figures associated with , specifically discussing whether Elon Musk should face investigation. Jeffries previously framed Democrats ' midterm win as a mandate to "fight MAGA extremism," though the term remains undefined and could broadly apply to Trump administration policies supported by 2024 voters. Musk has become a frequent target for Democrats since buying Twitter and rebranding it as X, with critics citing his wealth, his platform changes, and SpaceX's federal contracts, even as some protesters have resorted to vandalizing Tesla dealerships in response. Latest tech failure hits America 's farmers The USDA has experienced multiple system outages since Monday after its Cybersecurity and Privacy Operations Center forcing a reset of database passwords and affecting farmer loan and financial aid programs. | | ---|---|--- The disruption adds to a wave of recent tech outages nationwide affecting banks, airlines, and other systems; Trump has dismissed the idea of a coordinated foreign cyberattack, calling the incidents isolated, even as the administration searches for a new national cyber director. USDA officials gave conflicting explanations, with one attributing outages to routine software updates while internal guidance warned staff of continued intermittent disruptions. Marsha Blackburn won the governor's office on November 3, and the headline writers treated it like a formality: first female governor in Tennessee history, Republican, done. But look one line down on the results table and you'll find the real story of this election. Blackburn took 45.5 percent of the vote -- a 2.6-point margin over Jerri Green, a Memphis city councilwoman, and the closest gubernatorial race in Tennessee since 1896. An independent businessman, David Hatley, finished at 9.3 percent, with a dozen more independents on the ballot behind him. Four years earlier, Bill Lee won this office by thirty points. The race shifted twenty-seven points toward the Democrats from the 2024 presidential baseline in a single cycle.
Something in the Tennessee electorate broke this month. The fracture line runs through the registration rolls, and it runs straight back to the moving trucks.

# This is a big win for clean air and environmental justice.
For too long, the Reworld incinerator has endangered the health of people in the entire region but _especially for the majority Black, working class community of Chester._ Through our persistent organizing efforts, we delivered a big setback to Mayor Cherelle Parker’s administration that had proposed renewing the Reworld contract for up to seven years.
We asked for your support and you came through! Community members filled the hearing room as they testified in front of the Council for hours ahead of the vote. Altogether with our organizing partners — CIRQL, 215 People's alliance, Reclaim, Clean Air Council, and Trash Academy — we were able to win and cut our contract with Reworld". One Pa delivered **8,000 petition signatures** to Mayor Parker and City Council in opposition to renewing the Reworld contract.
Thanks for having the community’s back and putting the pressure on City Council to make the right choice.
You made this victory possible. _**[Consider chipping in towards our next big fights so we have the resources for what comes next.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143771642/661350509/-1740112309?refcode=EM_FL_OPA_20261120_fr_STOAwin_team_oc_act_xx_l1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vQ1BELzEvMTEzNTk1IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjI5OTcxYmJmLTAyZTUtZjExMS05MWYzLTAwMGQzYTUzMzk3OCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=FPsV8mbOLHVWjljCmrdl2YkK-OMaWrQVJ-MkvXzgCpk=)**_

It’s been a busy week. I’ve been working to deliver for families in New Mexico and across the country. This week, I secured **over $400 million for New Mexico** in the Senate’s new funding bills for 2027. Now, let me be clear, I do have real concerns about certain things Senate Republicans put into — or kept out of — these bills. And I am going to keep fighting to get these fixed. But once Congress finishes negotiating these bills, the money I fought to include for New Mexico will help families put food on the table and find a home they can afford. It will deliver mental health support for kids, help for survivors of domestic violence, care for our veterans, and clean water to communities that have waited far too long for it. Now, the path ahead requires fighting against a stubborn MAGA GOP that refused to give rural communities the help they need, rein in an out-of-control ICE, and fund Congress’s power to hold this administration accountable. **New Mexicans deserve better than that. I’m going to keep working to lower costs, create good-paying jobs, and bring investments home to our communities.** When I’m in Washington, it matters to know supporters like you have my back at home. **[If you support the work I’m doing for New Mexico, will you add your name?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143772494/661353259/-96707208?refcode=AU_MTH_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20261120_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2M2E3NGRmNS0wM2U1LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=s6xN4EBLf4UOK5nlnMvi0HpbzlpCl97wcOx0cZhh7qs=&emci=60a74df5-03e5-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=63a74df5-03e5-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=252045)** | [ADD YOUR NAME](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143772495/661353260/-96707208?refcode=AU_MTH_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20261120_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2M2E3NGRmNS0wM2U1LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=s6xN4EBLf4UOK5nlnMvi0HpbzlpCl97wcOx0cZhh7qs=&emci=60a74df5-03e5-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=63a74df5-03e5-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=252045)

#### _**[Elon Musk spent years using his money and influence to shape American politics. Now, as Democrats prepare to take power in Congress, he's reportedly looking for a way back into their good graces. That's why independent media matters. At Endless Urgency, we're asking the questions powerful people would rather avoid, following the money, and demanding accountability from both parties. No corporate interests deciding what we can say. Just you, me, and a commitment to telling the truth. * * *
I was on NewsNation last night with Leland Vittert, and he asked me a question I've been chewing on since: Should Democrats take Elon Musk's money now that he's suddenly decided he's not MAGA? Should we welcome his support with open arms?
Absolutely not. And frankly, any Democrat who does should be primaried.
Let's be clear about what's happening here, because it's staggeringly pathetic. Elon Musk is now telling the world he was never really MAGA. This is the same man who proudly declared himself MAGA over and over again. The same man who wore all the stupid hats. The same man who worked inside Donald Trump's administration and spent ungodly amounts of money trying to elect MAGA candidates across this country. The same man who donated over 20 million dollars worth of his SpaceX stocks to 'Trump accounts' to escape billions in capital gains taxes. And now, two weeks after Democrats wiped the floor with Republicans in the midterms, he wants us to believe he was just a curious bystander the whole time?
He's not alone. Alex Karp from Palantir is out here claiming he was secretly progressive all along. Peter Thiel says he opposed the war in Iran, even though he never said a word about it while his handpicked puppet, J.D. Vance, gleefully went along with it for the better part of a year.
You have to be a special kind of stupid to believe these people weren't active, willing participants in the corruption, chaos, and depravity of the last two years. They bankrolled it. They profited from it. And they should be held accountable just like anybody else.
And why do you think they're all suddenly trying to play nice with Democrats? I'll tell you why. Because Democrats are preparing to investigate the hell out of them. There are reports that congressional Democrats are already targeting Musk's companies, Apple, and Meta, with investigations into everything from government contracts and corporate dealings with Trump to the use of Musk's AI technology in military operations. Corporate executives are scrambling to lawyer up, and Musk himself is reportedly bracing for a barrage of subpoenas. You think these guys aren't nervous about what investigators might uncover? Give me a fucking break.
Make no mistake: people like Elon Musk created the affordability crisis you're living through right now. They abused our government for their own gain. They gutted critical services so they could get their tax cuts. And they helped put a fascist regime in power that doesn't give a damn about you or me and only cares about stuffing money into their back pockets. We've witnessed one of the greatest transfers of wealth in American history, from working people to the richest few, who now hold wealth, power, and influence on a scale this country has never seen.
And if they've committed crimes, they need to answer for them. I believe Elon Musk has. At a minimum, he should be investigated for trying to buy votes in last year's Wisconsin Supreme Court race. He should be investigated for what he did at DOGE, which I believe was criminal. He handed our most personal, sensitive information to a bunch of young idiots conservatives. Absolutely insane.
Thankfully, our democracy still works well enough that we overcame the obscene money Musk, Trump, and their friends spent. We elected great Democrats like James Talarico, Annie Andrews, Scott Colom, Josh Turek, Mary Peltola, and so many others. Voters handed us the House and the Senate and delivered victories in places like Texas, Mississippi, Alaska, and Ohio. That wasn't just a mandate for change. It was a directive: rein these people in, expose the corruption, and fix the affordability crisis they created.
But winning doesn't mean we get to rest on our laurels. And it sure as hell doesn't mean we get to make nice with these guys just because they've started saying nice things about Democrats.
Musk is reportedly hiring a team of high-powered, Democratic-aligned lobbyists to ingratiate himself with our party. We have to resist that with every fiber of our being.
That raises a pretty obvious question: What exactly is he hoping to get in return? Access? Influence? A carte blanche with the people who are supposed to be investigating what happened inside his government operation? My guess is all of the above.
Democrats cannot cozy up to the very people who created the crisis that delivered us these victories in the first place. That would be extraordinarily stupid. Voters didn't send us to Washington so we could turn around and cash Elon Musk's checks.
* * *
#### _**[This is what keeps me up at night. Not just whether Congress investigates Elon Musk or whether another billionaire gets hauled in front of a committee. It's whether any of it actually changes something for the people who have lost faith in our government. Accountability has to mean something. So does winning. And independent media has a responsibility to keep asking the hard questions, even when the people in power are Democrats. That's the promise I'm making with Endless Urgency. Your $8/month helps us keep this newsletter free for everyone, and continue covering the decisions that affect your life without answering to the wealthy people making them.](https://substack.com/redirect/f0f312bb-25fb-40a9-aa4f-8119020df4f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_

* * *
Here's the part where I have to be honest with you. Leland was skeptical that anything would change. He doubted Democrats would get serious about holding Musk or anybody else accountable, and suggested these investigations would amount to nothing but pissing off the American people.
It's hard to argue with him. For a very long time, Democrats have been performative. They've been unwilling to go after the people robbing you of your dignity and shrinking your paycheck, and unwilling to do the hard, transformational things at a moment when Americans are crying out for change.
I share that skepticism. I'm worried, too.
The American people agree with us on the vast majority of issues. They just don't believe the Democratic Party can deliver for them.
Many are giving up on the system altogether, because no matter who wins, very little changes and nobody ever gets held accountable.
And that's a much bigger problem than any one election. When people stop believing their government is capable of making their lives better, they start questioning whether participating in the political process makes any difference at all.
If that happens again, the pendulum swings right back, we elect another Republican president, and all these incredible young voices we're excited about get wiped out in a couple of years.
So here's what Democrats need to do in January. Subpoena every record from DOGE and find out exactly who got access to your data. Investigate what happened in Wisconsin and investigate Musk's government contracts and abuses of power. Pass a ban on congressional stock trading, real campaign finance reform, and simple, easy-to-understand bills that lower costs, and force Trump to veto them in front of the whole country. And refuse money from corrupt billionaires, full stop.
That also means cleaning our own house. Democrats have their own serious questions to answer about insider trading, conflicts of interest, and their relationships with powerful people, including individuals from our own party being named in the Epstein files.
If we want credibility on corruption, we can't look away when it's one of ours. The party that moves first to clean up this broken government is the party the American people will reward.
It'll lead to a lot of uncomfortable conversations, and a lot of Washington Post editorialists clutching their pearls about "lawfare."
Fuck all that noise. Go do the work voters sent you there to do.
Because the point of winning power isn't to protect the people who already have it. It's to do something worthwhile for those who have entrusted you with it.
I'm going to use this newsletter, my platforms, and every connection I have to push Democrats in the right direction. And I'll be at the front of the line calling them out when they don't.

With urgency,
--Mike

clean_body: The men and women of our military deserve better than Pete Hegseth. | | | | Welcome back to Fact Friday. Today we're talking about Pete Hegseth. The fact of the matter is that Pete Hegseth has been nothing but a complete and utter embarrassment to our country and to the men and women who put their lives on the line to serve it. Pete Hegseth should never have been confirmed as Secretary of Defense in the first place. He is unqualified, incompetent, and unserious. Under his inept leadership, our country has been plunged into an unnecessary and illegal war; he's lied about its success and has no credible plan to end it. To make matters worse, nearly 900 service members have been injured, and 23 American heroes have died. In truth, this number may be much higher, but Hegseth's Department of Defense has tried to categorize these deaths in a way that obscures the real truth and impact of this war. As long as Pete Hegseth remains in his position, America and her service members are in harm's way. After his confirmation, with inconceivable arrogance and reckless abandon, he fired dozens of highly qualified, high-level military officials to protect his ego. It's clear that Pete Hegseth is in way over his head and must be removed from power immediately. Our service members, our country, and our allies deserve a Secretary of Defense who respects the law and understands the gravity of this office, not someone who gambles with America's safety just to inflate his sense of self. For these reasons and many, many more, I will continue to call for Pete Hegseth to be impeached immediately. If you want to keep getting clear, fact-based breakdowns of the issues affecting our community, make sure you stay connected and share this with someone who should be paying attention, too. It is not lost on me that this strain may be particularly difficult to bear as people everywhere prepare to gather around the Thanksgiving table. ## **Policy Needs to Be Personal: The One Lesson Republicans Must Master Now**
As we step back from this election cycle and look toward the next two years on Capitol Hill, one strategic takeaway needs to capture the mindset of every single Republican in Washington: **policy needs to be personal.**
During my time in the West Wing and on campaigns, I watched lawmakers fall into the same trap time and time again. We talk in legislative abstracts, budget figures, and Washington shorthand - completely forgetting to connect what we are doing to how it actually affects a family's daily life.
[| | | | | Echelon Insights
---
@EchelonInsights
COSTS DROVE 2026: Republicans and Independents gave cost of living the most often for explaining the GOP's defeat in the 2026 midterm.
| 7:37 PM * Nov 17, 2026 * 1.29K Views1 Repost * 3 Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/101c98ff-6b2d-458e-b5b8-575f8101ec94?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Think about what happens when we talk about our own agenda:
* **Fighting Waste and Fraud:** You don't go after government fraud just for the sake of a committee hearing. You go after it because that fraud is driving up prices and taking money directly out of taxpayers' pockets.
* **Permitting Reform:** Nobody outside of Capitol Hill gets excited about '"permitting reform" for its own sake - especially as Congress debates major permitting bills like the Bipartisan Affordability and American Jobs Act. You push it because cutting red tape creates good-paying jobs, lowers utility bills, and helps families build a better life.
* **Healthcare Reform:** It isn't just about debating policy frameworks in Washington. It is about bringing down monthly premiums and out-of-pocket costs - which make up one of the biggest burdens on a family's household budget.

Every single issue we champion has to pass one simple test: _How does this make an everyday person 's life more affordable, easier, or more efficient? _
And that rule applies just as much to how we play offense in the minority as it does to our own legislative proposals.

subject: He wants $50 billion more
body:
|
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143774062/661359495/-1160839820?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkwNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMjEyYTE1YS0wNWU1LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=FfN0IDiOybG5CRM4VQhnVDsHL-4FegI5aLvzQPT8_po=)
Peter, If you were trying to catch a plane this past weekend, there’s a good chance you spent more time at the gate than in the air. A nationwide ground stop left travelers stuck at airports across the country for hours. In twenty years as a meteorologist, I watched plenty of storms ripple across the map and snarl air travel, so I know how much our day-to-day lives depend on that system running smoothly. But this time, there was no storm to blame. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says a contractor’s tech error triggered a systems outage. He’s also blaming Congress for not giving the FAA enough funding, and after months of asking for $30 billion, he’s now asking for $50 billion. **That’s rich. Back in 2019, Duffy voted against FAA funding when he was in Congress. And since becoming Transportation Secretary, he’s spent months away filming a reality TV show.** Seems like his priorities are a little mixed up. Dear Advocate for Life, Imagine a young woman who has just discovered she's pregnant. She's frightened, overwhelmed, and unsure of what to do next. Maybe she hasn't told anyone. Maybe someone in her life is pressuring her to have an abortion. But what if, before making that decision, she had the opportunity to see her baby for the very first time? **That's the life-changing opportunity your gift to PreBorn! can help provide.** Through our PreBorn! Network Clinics across America, mothers facing unexpected pregnancies receive free ultrasounds, compassionate care, and the opportunity to hear the gospel of Jesus Christ. When a mother sees her baby on the ultrasound screen and hears that tiny heartbeat, she has the opportunity to recognize the precious new life growing within her. **Your gift of just $28 helps provide one life-saving ultrasound and shares the hope of the gospel with a mother considering abortion.** And as our thank-you for your gift of any amount, we'll send you PreBorn!'s beautiful new **2027**** _Celebrate the Beauty of New Life_****Calendar!**

Network Clinics across America, mothers facing unexpected pregnancies receive free ultrasounds, compassionate care, and the opportunity to hear the gospel of Jesus Christ. | | | | Dear Advocate for Life, Imagine a young woman who has just discovered she's pregnant. She's frightened, overwhelmed, and unsure of what to do next. Maybe she hasn't told anyone. Maybe someone in her life is pressuring her to have an abortion. But what if, before making that decision, she had the opportunity to see her baby for the very first time? That's the life-changing opportunity your gift to PreBorn! can help provide. Through our PreBorn! Network Clinics across America, mothers facing unexpected pregnancies receive free ultrasounds, compassionate care, and the opportunity to hear the gospel of Jesus Christ. When a mother sees her baby on the ultrasound screen and hears that tiny heartbeat, she has the opportunity to recognize the precious new life growing within her. Your gift of just $28 helps provide one life-saving ultrasound and shares the hope of the gospel with a mother considering abortion. And as our thank-you for your gift of any amount, we'll send you PreBorn!'s beautiful new 2027 Celebrate the Beauty of New LifeCalendar! Filled with stunning photography, encouraging Scriptures, and space to record your prayers and blessings, this special calendar celebrates God's goodness and the extraordinary gift of every human life. It also includes a 2027 Ministry Prayer Guide to help you pray for mothers, babies, and the ongoing work of PreBorn! throughout the year. Every new life is worth celebrating. Will you help protect the next one? Gratefully, The PreBorn! Team Pop Acta Media | Inside Scoop Politics PO Box 2221 Fort Collins, CO 80522 | _

## Is the US Under Cyber Attack?
This week has been rife with outages at Microsoft, the FAA, banks, Apple, and more. It has many of us wondering what exactly is going on. Are these outages connected? Are AI agents on the loose? Well, the answer is probably a bit complicated. For the past several years, there have been mass layoffs all across the tech industry as workers are replaced with AI. As programmers start to rely more on AI for coding, hackers use AI to uncover vulnerabilities, and cybersecurity researchers use AI to patch bugs, instability grows. We believe that this past week we've been seeing the results of that instability in the form of the many outages we've been seeing. Of course, this is all speculation on our part, as the only things we know for sure are what the companies experiencing the outages have told us. Do not click any links. Instead, just close your browser.

| Microsoft Outage Does Not Appear to Be Cyber Attack
---
Last week there was a major outage with Microsoft's 365 suite of services that affected businesses around the world. You might have heard about it. Many professional workplaces rely on Microsoft services like Teams and Outlook for day-to-day operations, and the outage, which lasted almost 24 hours, impacted many businesses. Workplaces in Japan broke out their [fax machines and landlines](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17250-261862-8928135-ab8ddf38cd-4s726ae7a5) to keep operations running.Microsoft's [preliminary report](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17250-261862-8928136-5135a1e06e-4s726ae7a5) has traced the source of the outage to a change that was deployed to its servers over the summer. The change had been tested on older, less powerful hardware, so a bug that only occurs under certain conditions related to CPU and memory usage was not detected. When the change was made to newer servers, it caused them to stop responding. Essentially, as traffic reached its peak, the traffic was redirected to other servers, all of which continued to lock up. Read the full technical breakdown at [Ars Technica](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17250-261862-8928137-c9ad348668-4s726ae7a5).**The Bottom Line** : Despite worries about a cyber attack, the Microsoft outage was due to a bug in how its servers work. More rigorous testing from Microsoft could have prevented this outage, since the bug would have been more easily detectable if it had been tested on the right hardware.

## FAA Says Ground Stop Not Related to AI System
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a [nationwide ground stop](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17250-261862-8928138-23d28ffdc1-4s726ae7a5) last Friday, preventing any planes in the US from taking off. Perhaps coincidentally, the FAA rolled out a new [AI-powered system](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17250-261862-8928139-1e641f751f-4s726ae7a5), called Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories (SMART), on November 10, just days before the ground stop. The FAA insists that the ground stop was unrelated to SMART or, for that matter, any cyber attack. According to Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy, the FAA's telecommunications routers were completely overwhelmed, causing them to shut down. He did not say what they were overwhelmed by, and [experts widely speculate](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17250-261862-8928140-e8e3d501e3-4s726ae7a5) that it was the SMART system.**The Bottom Line** : The FAA briefly tested SMART in the Washington area before deploying it nationwide. The timing of the ground stop with the deployment of this new AI system without more rigorous testing is certainly interesting, though we can't know for sure whether or not it was the cause. A more thorough investigation would yield more concrete answers, though an [investigation at this point is unlikely](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17250-261862-8928141-3ce44de121-4s726ae7a5). As with the Microsoft outage, there is no evidence that hackers were involved.
## Multiple US Banks Experience Outages
It would seem the theme of this past week is outages, as banks across the US experienced an outage following Microsoft and the FAA. Customers at Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and others reported issues with accessing their accounts as well as with transferring money using Zelle. The parent company of Chase, JPMorganChase, has stated that it was experiencing a "systemic issue," not a cybersecurity issue. It also believes that the outages experienced by other banks were due to transactions with JPMorganChase. Read more at [Wired](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17250-261862-8928142-269e633135-4s726ae7a5).**The Bottom Line** : Once again, it does not appear that these outages were related to a cyber attack. JPMorganChase has not specified what the systemic issue was that caused the outage, but it is working to resolve the issue.

## Cyber Attack Puts Hundreds of Websites at Risk
While we have had three outages unrelated to cyber attacks, an actual cyber attack has affected a number of websites, including CNN, BBC, Zoom, Ikea, Equifax, and many others. The attack is a supply chain attack targeting Optimizely, an AI software platform used for testing websites. Hackers have injected malicious code into nearly 200 websites, attempting to steal payment and cryptocurrency information. Read more at [Newsweek](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17250-261862-8928144-1d1cdb8d7b-4s726ae7a5).**The Bottom Line** : Optimizely has already deployed a patch for the vulnerability that allowed the hackers to do this. It has also removed the malicious code from the affected websites, so there's not much for you to do. However, if you visited any of the infected websites and logged into an account on November 16, there is a risk that any payment information associated with your account could have been exposed. The Newsweek article linked above has a list of the impacted websites.

## Can Hackers Steal Your Face?
Last week, we reported on a story about North Korean hackers making off with over $6 billion worth of cryptocurrency. The FBI has [seized $1.2 billion](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17250-261862-8928146-e503da5638-4s726ae7a5) of the stolen crypto, but is now warning about a new North Korean-run scam called FaceStealer. The scam works by tricking victims into joining a video call that looks like a legitimate Zoom or Teams meeting, where the scammers can then use the webcam footage and AI to create deepfakes of the victim. They can then use the victim's face to trick friends, family members, or coworkers into installing malware on their computers over video call. Read more at [Patch](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17250-261862-8928147-2607920c4a-4s726ae7a5).**The Bottom Line** : At the moment, it appears FaceStealer is primarily targeted at those who own large amounts of cryptocurrency, but the FBI believes the hackers could be expanding their efforts. You can avoid becoming a victim of FaceStealer by verifying meeting invitations before you join and keeping your webcam off until you see the other person who invited you to the meeting. Don't accept unsolicited meeting invitations over third-party services like WhatsApp or Telegram.
## How Militaries Use Facial Recognition Technology
The Israeli military has been found to be using an AI-powered facial recognition platform owned by Amazon called Rekognition. Since at least 2024, the military has been feeding Rekognition millions of images of Palestinians and using that information to monitor them. According to the military, it is using this technology to identify militants. Check out the full story at [The Guardian](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17250-261862-8928148-5a1475b822-4s726ae7a5).**The Bottom Line** : No matter what it's being used for, facial recognition technology has been proven to be unreliable. It is prone to mistakes, not to mention the privacy violations involved in capturing images of someone's face and feeding them to AI.

## Data Breach Affects Uber Drivers
Uber is the latest victim of a data breach, with nearly 150,000 drivers affected. The hackers responsible for this breach used compromised credentials to access a third-party service provider. They stole images of Uber drivers' licenses, names, addresses, ID numbers, and more. The victims are being notified and offered free credit monitoring. Check out the full story at [SecurityWeek](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17250-261862-8928150-7bb9bf5236-4s726ae7a5).**The Bottom Line** : This breach only affects drivers who work for Uber. If you're an Uber driver and were affected by this breach, you should have already heard from the company by now. This breach likely occurred due to reused credentials, which is why we so often recommend using a password manager to ensure every password you use is unique.
## Meta Threatens to Pull Encryption Services from Canada
We've reported on Canada's C-22 bill a couple of times already. It's a new bill that would require tech companies to integrate surveillance capabilities into their systems, even if they're encrypted like Apple's Advanced Data Protection. Encrypted messaging service [Signal has threatened to pull out of Canada](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17250-261862-8928151-39655b8df0-4s726ae7a5) if the bill passes, and the parent company of Facebook, Meta, is joining them. Meta has said that it will consider pulling its encryption services from Canada if C-22 is allowed to pass. Read more at [CBC](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17250-261862-8928152-d36ae2f9c2-4s726ae7a5).**The Bottom Line** : We see the C-22 bill as a threat to digital privacy and security and appreciate any tech companies standing up to it. If you live in Canada and feel similarly, we recommend reaching out to your representatives to voice your concerns.
## Toll Text Scams on the Rise Once More
Unpaid toll texts or emails are a common scam tactic that had started to cool off over the past year, but appear to be picking up steam again just in time for the holiday season. This scam works similarly to the [post package scam](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17250-261862-8928131-5f4f2a382a-4s726ae7a5): you receive a text or email letting you know that you have an unpaid toll, usually an E-ZPass toll. The message will provide a link where you can make the payment. Stay informed on how to counter the unpaid toll scam at [Fox News](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17250-261862-8928153-1fccf26b2b-4s726ae7a5).**The Bottom Line** : Of course, if you open the link in the text or email, you'll be taken to a malicious web page that is designed to look legitimate. And if you make the payment, your money will just be going to the scammer. Not only that, but they'll also have access to any payment details you entered on the malicious web page. This type of scam is bound to become more popular as the holidays approach, and people start traveling more often.

## What Is the Most Common Password?
NordPass has released its annual report of the most commonly used passwords, and you'll never guess what's sitting at number one. It turns out, "123456" is the most used password in the world, followed swiftly by "admin" and "12345678." You'd think everyone would know by now not to use easily guessed passwords like this, but it is still common practice. Find out what other passwords people are using at [The Register](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17250-261862-8928154-571092f1d3-4s726ae7a5).**The Bottom Line** : We can only assume that the logic behind using "123456" as a password is that it's so simple; why would anyone guess it? Except password cracking software can figure this password out in seconds, not to mention that the advent of AI has sped up the process considerably. Using a password manager can greatly mitigate the risk of having your password stolen. Password managers are designed to generate passwords made of random words or characters, making it as difficult as possible for computers to guess. Of course, making a password unique also makes it hard to remember, but thankfully, password managers also save every password you create. If you need a best [password manager recommendation](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17250-261862-8928155-59b196edf4-4s726ae7a5), we can help you decide. If you're already using a password manager, great! Keep using the one you're most familiar with.

The correct answer is **B. Delete the text and report it as spam**. E-ZPass does not send text messages about unpaid tolls; it sends notices through the mail. This is a common scam tactic, and if you open the link in the text, you'll be taken to a malicious web page where you'll be directed to enter payment information. That information will not go to E-ZPass; it will be sent to the scammers. However, there are some toll authorities that will send text messages, which is where it becomes difficult to tell real texts from the scams. As programmers start to rely more on AI for coding, hackers use AI to uncover vulnerabilities, and cybersecurity researchers use AI to patch bugs, instability grows. We believe that this past week we've been seeing the results of that instability in the form of the many outages we've been seeing. What should you do? 🤔 1. Follow the instructions in the text to pay off your toll. 2. Delete the text and report it as spam. 3. Contact E-ZPass. Scroll to the bottom to see how you did! | Microsoft Outage Does Not Appear to Be Cyber Attack Last week there was a major outage with Microsoft's 365 suite of services that affected businesses around the world. You might have heard about it. Many professional workplaces rely on Microsoft services like Teams and Outlook for day-to-day operations, and the outage, which lasted almost 24 hours, impacted many businesses. Workplaces in Japan broke out their to keep operations running.Microsoft's has traced the source of the outage to a change that was deployed to its servers over the summer. The change had been tested on older, less powerful hardware, so a bug that only occurs under certain conditions related to CPU and memory usage was not detected. When the change was made to newer servers, it caused them to stop responding. Essentially, as traffic reached its peak, the traffic was redirected to other servers, all of which continued to lock up. Read the full technical breakdown at Bottom Line : Despite worries about a cyber attack, the Microsoft outage was due to a bug in how its servers work. More rigorous testing from Microsoft could have prevented this outage, since the bug would have been more easily detectable if it had been tested on the right hardware. | | | In Partnership with NativePath Easy bruising may be a clue worth paying attention to. | 🤨 This Should Be on Your Radar 📡 FAA Says Ground Stop Not Related to AI System The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a last Friday, preventing any planes in the US from taking off. Perhaps coincidentally, the FAA rolled out a new , called Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories (SMART), on November 10, just days before the ground stop. The FAA insists that the ground stop was unrelated to SMART or, for that matter, any cyber attack. According to Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy, the FAA's telecommunications routers were completely overwhelmed, causing them to shut down. He did not say what they were overwhelmed by, and that it was the SMART system.The Bottom Line : The FAA briefly tested SMART in the Washington area before deploying it nationwide. The timing of the ground stop with the deployment of this new AI system without more rigorous testing is certainly interesting, though we can't know for sure whether or not it was the cause. A more thorough investigation would yield more concrete answers, though an . As with the Microsoft outage, there is no evidence that hackers were involved. Multiple US Banks Experience Outages It would seem the theme of this past week is outages, as banks across the US experienced an outage following Microsoft and the FAA. Customers at Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and others reported issues with accessing their accounts as well as with transferring money using Zelle. The parent company of Chase, JPMorganChase, has stated that it was experiencing a "systemic issue," not a cybersecurity issue. It also believes that the outages experienced by other banks were due to transactions with JPMorganChase. Read more at Bottom Line : Once again, it does not appear that these outages were related to a cyber attack. JPMorganChase has not specified what the systemic issue was that caused the outage, but it is working to resolve the issue. | | | | | | In Partnership with Finance Buzz If you have outstanding credit card debt, getting a new 0% intro APR credit card could help ease the pressure while you pay down your balances. Our credit card experts identified top credit cards that are perfect for anyone looking to pay down debt and not add to it! | Cyber Attack Puts Hundreds of Websites at Risk While we have had three outages unrelated to cyber attacks, an actual cyber attack has affected a number of websites, including CNN, BBC, Zoom, Ikea, Equifax, and many others. The attack is a supply chain attack targeting Optimizely, an AI software platform used for testing websites. Hackers have injected malicious code into nearly 200 websites, attempting to steal payment and cryptocurrency information. Read more at Bottom Line : Optimizely has already deployed a patch for the vulnerability that allowed the hackers to do this. It has also removed the malicious code from the affected websites, so there's not much for you to do. However, if you visited any of the infected websites and logged into an account on November 16, there is a risk that any payment information associated with your account could have been exposed. The Newsweek article linked above has a list of the impacted websites. How Secure Is Apple's HomeView? Apple's HomeView device is now available! HomeView is designed to be able to detect up to six different people who use the device. It does this using something called ambient sensing, which relies on the camera and microphone. Having an always-on camera and microphone in your home can be concerning (to say the least), which is why Apple has and how it works with ambient sensing. Check it out if you're interested.The Bottom Line : We're not big fans of having an always-on camera or microphone in our homes, but we appreciate Apple's transparency when it comes to this technology. | | | In Partnership with Finance Buzz Our that are perfect for anyone looking to pay down debt and not add to it! | Can Hackers Steal Your Face? Last week, we reported on a story about North Korean hackers making off with over $6 billion worth of cryptocurrency. The FBI has of the stolen crypto, but is now warning about a new North Korean-run scam called FaceStealer. The scam works by tricking victims into joining a video call that looks like a legitimate Zoom or Teams meeting, where the scammers can then use the webcam footage and AI to create deepfakes of the victim. They can then use the victim's face to trick friends, family members, or coworkers into installing malware on their computers over video call. Read more at Bottom Line : At the moment, it appears FaceStealer is primarily targeted at those who own large amounts of cryptocurrency, but the FBI believes the hackers could be expanding their efforts. You can avoid becoming a victim of FaceStealer by verifying meeting invitations before you join and keeping your webcam off until you see the other person who invited you to the meeting. Don't accept unsolicited meeting invitations over third-party services like WhatsApp or Telegram. How Militaries Use Facial Recognition Technology The Israeli military has been found to be using an AI-powered facial recognition platform owned by Amazon called Rekognition. Since at least 2024, the military has been feeding Rekognition millions of images of Palestinians and using that information to monitor them. According to the military, it is using this technology to identify militants. Check out the full story at Bottom Line : No matter what it's being used for, facial recognition technology has been proven to be unreliable. It is prone to mistakes, not to mention the privacy violations involved in capturing images of someone's face and feeding them to AI. | | | | | | In Partnership with Lumo AI Lumo is Proton's for writing, research, planning and image creation. It runs on European infrastructure, locks saved chats with zero-access encryption and never trains on your conversations. today! | Data Breach Affects Uber Drivers Uber is the latest victim of a data breach, with nearly 150,000 drivers affected. The hackers responsible for this breach used compromised credentials to access a third-party service provider. They stole images of Uber drivers' licenses, names, addresses, ID numbers, and more. The victims are being notified and offered free credit monitoring. Check out the full story at Bottom Line : This breach only affects drivers who work for Uber. If you're an Uber driver and were affected by this breach, you should have already heard from the company by now. This breach likely occurred due to reused credentials, which is why we so often recommend using a password manager to ensure every password you use is unique. Meta Threatens to Pull Encryption Services from Canada We've reported on Canada's C-22 bill a couple of times already. It's a new bill that would require tech companies to integrate surveillance capabilities into their systems, even if they're encrypted like Apple's Advanced Data Protection. Encrypted messaging service if the bill passes, and the parent company of Facebook, Meta, is joining them. Meta has said that it will consider pulling its encryption services from Canada if C-22 is allowed to pass. Read more at Bottom Line : We see the C-22 bill as a threat to digital privacy and security and appreciate any tech companies standing up to it. If you live in Canada and feel similarly, we recommend reaching out to your representatives to voice your concerns. Toll Text Scams on the Rise Once More Unpaid toll texts or emails are a common scam tactic that had started to cool off over the past year, but appear to be picking up steam again just in time for the holiday season. This scam works similarly to the : you receive a text or email letting you know that you have an unpaid toll, usually an E-ZPass toll. The message will provide a link where you can make the payment. Stay informed on how to counter the unpaid toll scam at Bottom Line : Of course, if you open the link in the text or email, you'll be taken to a malicious web page that is designed to look legitimate. And if you make the payment, your money will just be going to the scammer. Not only that, but they'll also have access to any payment details you entered on the malicious web page. This type of scam is bound to become more popular as the holidays approach, and people start traveling more often. | | | In Partnership with Lumo AI Lumo is Proton’s for writing, research, planning and image creation. Save 23% on the annual Lumo... | 🙈 Security Fail of the Week 👎 What Is the Most Common Password? NordPass has released its annual report of the most commonly used passwords, and you'll never guess what's sitting at number one. It turns out, "123456" is the most used password in the world, followed swiftly by "admin" and "12345678." You'd think everyone would know by now not to use easily guessed passwords like this, but it is still common practice. Find out what other passwords people are using at Bottom Line : We can only assume that the logic behind using "123456" as a password is that it's so simple; why would anyone guess it? Except password cracking software can figure this password out in seconds, not to mention that the advent of AI has sped up the process considerably. Using a password manager can greatly mitigate the risk of having your password stolen. Password managers are designed to generate passwords made of random words or characters, making it as difficult as possible for computers to guess. Of course, making a password unique also makes it hard to remember, but thankfully, password managers also save every password you create. If you need a best , we can help you decide. If you're already using a password manager, great! Keep using the one you're most familiar with. | 🍎📱 Security Updates from Apple 🍎 The most recent iOS and iPadOS is 27.2.1 The most recent macOS is 27.2.1 The most recent tvOS is 27.2.1 The most recent watchOS is 27.2.1 The most recent visionOS is 27.2.1 Read about the latest . | Security Skills Answer The correct answer is B. Delete the text and report it as spam. E-ZPass does not send text messages about unpaid tolls; it sends notices through the mail. This is a common scam tactic, and if you open the link in the text, you'll be taken to a malicious web page where you'll be directed to enter payment information. That information will not go to E-ZPass; it will be sent to the scammers. However, there are some toll authorities that will send text messages, which is where it becomes difficult to tell real texts from the scams. The FCC has a handy guide to help you determine when you're dealing with a scam text. | Mission Statement There is far too much security and privacy news for us to cover it all. | | | Hi Peter, When first elected to serve as Caucus Chair four years ago, my chief aim was to flip ten seats and break the Republican supermajority in the Tennessee House. Today, thanks to your generous support, we’re only four seats away from that goal and restoring a modicum of balance of power to our state legislature. To protect our six newly flipped seats and flip the final four in 2028, other caucus leaders and I have already started laying the groundwork. New member orientation, candidate recruitment, and of course, fundraising are all underway. Our work began the morning after Election Day, and it won’t end until Democrats win the majority. We are fortunate to have so many of you who have been part of this years-long effort by our side. You have put in the hours, made the calls, knocked on the doors, raised the money, and continued showing up even when the road ahead seemed difficult. **We appreciate you, we see you, and we know how much you have invested in this fight.** None of that work or generosity is taken for granted, and we would not be where we are today without you. Our fight to build a better Tennessee is far from over. **[That's why we're asking you to become a monthly sustaining donor.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143777885/661369738/-1171516177?refcode=nov_midmonth&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82ODcxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjODU5N2I0MC0wY2U1LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=W9pdrLMkYE4reVtCcO4x2vxc00E3HxjnVjbB81inYdo=)** A recurring monthly contribution, at whatever level works for you, gives us the resources and stability to continue building on our momentum year-round. It allows us to plan ahead, invest early, support candidates, and compete in districts that will be critical to breaking the Republican supermajority. By now you know that, as Chair, I make sure that your money goes straight into strategically targeted campaigns. This past election cycle, our caucus, through the guidance of our caucus campaign committee, invested almost $700,000 in targeted House races across Tennessee. Every Democratic candidate who flipped a seat, won an open seat and won reelection to a vulnerable seat received significant financial support from our caucus. Three candidates who lost incredibly close elections also received financial support.

Mohammed Al-Mashkour Ali stands beside his grain mill at the Al-Lafa market in south Khartoum on November 16, 2026. Prolonged power outages following recent drone strikes on Sudan's electricity infrastructure have forced him to work alone overnight during the limited hours electricity is available. Photo by Aunnab Alman.
_Story by Aunnab Alman_
KHARTOUM, Sudan--In what has become an increasingly frequent feature of daily life in large swathes of Sudan, Afifa Mohammed spent most of Tuesday in her small home in Al-Asal south of Khartoum without electricity. The power went out at 10 a.m. and did not return until close to midnight.
Like millions of other Sudanese displaced by the country's brutal civil war, Mohammed was forced to flee her hometown of Bara, North Kordofan, with her children in March. Added to the hardship of displacement, she now has to contend with a lack of electricity.
She stays awake late into the night when power is available and rushes to complete tasks that require electricity--like pumping and storing water. The family now buys small quantities of food daily because they can no longer depend on refrigeration. There is no reliable schedule of power cuts. Some days, electricity comes on during the day before cutting out after sunset. Other days, the pattern is reversed.
Sudan's electricity network has been severely damaged over the last three and a half years of war with civilian infrastructure being targeted by both the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF). Yet a particularly intense wave of drone strikes at the end of October and into November targeting power stations, fuel supplies, and electricity infrastructure has brought the country's power grid to the brink of collapse. The United Nations children's agency (UNICEF) [warned](https://substack.com/redirect/0380cb17-b2b5-4b5f-863b-5f1857949c4c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) recently that not a day had passed during the last week of October without a drone striking a power station in Sudan.
"In just over two weeks between October 20 and November 4, 29 drone strikes, attributed to the Rapid Support Forces, hit electricity facilities and fuel stations across 11 states, triggering widespread power blackouts and further fuel shortages affecting millions far from the conflict frontlines," the United Nations Human Rights Office said in a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/7cfd814d-612e-47d3-bcaa-4ed66e0d0740?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) this week. "These drone strikes had a devastating impact on civilians and essential services, causing power outages that disrupted health services including dialysis and surgical procedures, access to clean water and food production."
Two weeks after the wave of attacks, major substations remain out of service. Repairing some of the country's most important power facilities could take months or longer, Shaker Ismail, an engineer with the Sudanese Electricity Company, told Drop Site News.
Across parts of the country, electricity is being rationed through planned cuts that do not adhere to a regular schedule, while hospitals, water systems, farms, and businesses struggle to operate on an already weakened grid. Replacement transformers must be manufactured abroad, spare parts are scarce, and the threat of further attacks is complicating efforts to restore power.
Ismail said the recent wave of attacks damaged some of the most difficult and expensive components to replace, including high-capacity transformers and digital control systems. Unlike smaller electrical equipment, the transformers cannot be purchased from local suppliers and instead must be manufactured to order in Europe or Asia to match the specifications of individual power stations. Manufacturing, shipping, and installation can take several months to more than a year, he added, particularly when equipment must be transported through a country torn apart by war.
A single large transformer can cost millions of dollars while Sudan's electricity authorities face shortages of foreign currency, Ismail said. Additional shortages in essential supplies, including cables, circuit breakers, and insulating oil, have exacerbated the crisis while reserve stocks have been depleted following the destruction of major warehouses in Khartoum.
The Sudanese military-backed government has accused the RSF of carrying out attacks on electricity infrastructure, and the UN also cited the RSF regarding the latest wave of strikes. While both warring parties have targeted civilians and committed human rights abuses, the RSF has been accused of the most serious crimes, including actions in the group's takeover of El Fasher in 2025 that bore "the hallmarks of genocide," according to a UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission for Sudan.
The conflict erupted in April 2023 when a long simmering rivalry between the two factions exploded into fighting. At least 150,000 people have been killed, with some estimates running far higher. Some 14 million have been forced from their homes and the International Rescue Committee says more people face famine in Sudan than in the rest of the world combined.
As the war between the SAF and the RSF continues to rage, the threat of renewed attacks has created another obstacle to restoring the power grid. According to Ismail, foreign companies and potential international donors are reluctant to finance repairs or send specialist engineers into areas where installations could be struck again.
One of Sudan's most important power stations, the Um Dabakir thermal power plant in White Nile State, was badly damaged in an October 29 strike that forced it to shut down. The station supplied major parts of White Nile and North Kordofan states, supported the wider grid serving Khartoum and Al-Jazirah, and provided electricity used by water-treatment facilities, hospitals, and agricultural projects, Ismail said.
Communities around Kosti, Rabak, and Al-Obeid, including large numbers of people displaced by the war, depend on services connected to the affected network. Restoring the station would require four replacement main transformers, reconstruction of its control room and electrical feeders, and maintenance of three damaged generating units, according to Ismail. He estimated that the repairs would cost tens of millions of dollars and take at least several months.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bdaba49b-59b3-4878-b8fb-e0335976e39a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Workers assess damage at the Al-Markhiyat power station north of Omdurman on October 28, 2026, following a drone strike on October 27. Photo by Ebrahim Hamid / AFP via Getty Images.
In Khartoum, the Al-Markhiyat substation west of Omdurman was also put out of service following a strike on October 27. The facility is a major connection point for electricity transmitted from Merowe Dam to Omdurman, Bahri, and parts of the capital. Its disruption also affected water infrastructure and hospitals connected to the network. Initial estimates suggested repairs could be completed within 10 days. But Ismail said the damage required imported transformers, high-voltage insulators, and other equipment unavailable locally. Affected areas continued to experience prolonged outages and scheduled power cuts as of this week.
The Sudan Electricity Holding Company and Ministry of Energy have yet to publicly announce the restoration of the major facilities damaged in the attacks. On November 15, distribution transformers were installed to restore supplies to Khartoum's Central Market and Local Market. But these localized interventions have not resolved the wider damage to the transmission network.
## **Effects Ranging from Dialysis to Agriculture**
At Abdullah Sheikh Al-Jumaih Hospital in Dongola, Northern State, power cuts have interrupted patients during dialysis treatment. Dr. Rasha Abdullah, a physician at the hospital, told Drop Site that a power cut in early November caused at least one dialysis machine's electrically powered blood pump to stop functioning, leaving blood in the tubing and filter at risk of clotting before it could be returned to the patient. Abdullah scrambled to use the machine's manual emergency mechanism to return the blood to the patient's circulation.
"The medical situation in the Northern State is critical, as hospitals rely on electricity for up to 98 per cent of their equipment and lighting," Abdullah said. She added that the power cuts have also disrupted the hospital's medicine storage.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fb6b8951-bf43-4c82-99fa-e99798a8a20d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Haemodialysis machines inside the Al-Asil Center in Dongola, Northern State, Sudan on November 19, 2026. During sudden power cuts this month when backup power failed, medical staff were forced to manually hand-crank the machines' blood pumps to return circulating blood to patients before it clotted, while power outages also forced the center to discard refrigerated stocks of essential anti-clotting heparin. Photo courtesy of Dr. Rasha Abdullah.
During one prolonged outage, the hospital's refrigeration systems stopped functioning for an entire day. With no alternative available, staff were forced to discard quantities of heparin, a medication used to prevent blood clotting during dialysis, because they could no longer ensure that the affected supplies had been stored under the proper conditions, Abdullah said.
Attacks on power infrastructure are also disrupting water supplies. "The right to water deteriorated significantly, particularly as prolonged electricity cuts, fuel shortages, attacks on infrastructure and disruptions to water-pumping systems affected access to safe drinking water," the UN Human Rights Office said in a recent report.
Workers and farmers across the economy are being affected by repeated blackouts.
At Al-Lafa market, south of Khartoum, grain mill owner Mohammed Al-Mashkour Ali said that after the recent wave of attacks, electricity in his area was available only between midnight and 7 a.m. He has taken to working alone at night, grinding as much grain as possible before customers arrived the following day.
"During the day, the electricity is completely cut off," Ali said. "Customers come to buy grain and have it ground, but I am unable to meet their demands."
He initially tried using a small generator, but rising fuel prices made it too expensive to operate. "In the early days, I tried relying on a small generator, but the rise in fuel prices caused me financial losses with little return, so I stopped," he said.
In Al-Jazirah State, farmer Sahar Mohammed said electricity shortages had disrupted the processing of agricultural products, even in areas where irrigation does not depend directly on the national grid. Mills and oil-processing facilities rely on electricity, while the cost of operating diesel-powered alternatives has increased. In Northern State, farmer Abu al-Qasim Muhammad Ahmad said the shutdown of the Al-Daba substation had left his area on an alternating electricity schedule: one day with power, followed by one day without it. He said the irregular pumping has damaged his alfalfa and orange crops.
Farmers who switched to diesel-powered irrigation faced higher costs and fuel shortages. Ahmad estimated that his production costs had doubled. He feared that continued disruptions would affect preparations for the winter growing season, particularly for crops of wheat and fava beans.
Sudan's electricity network had suffered extensive damage before the intense wave of drone strikes that began in late October. Before the latest attacks, national generation capacity had fallen from approximately 4,400 megawatts before the war to around 1,100 megawatts, according to the Associated Press.
Merowe Dam is now the last major power source in the country, providing more than 70% of the country's electricity and making transmission facilities that distribute its output to other parts of the country even more critical.
Ismail estimated that approximately 70% of Sudan's electricity infrastructure had been affected by the conflict and that the cost of repairing the wider network could exceed $3 billion, though he warned the lack of comprehensive records made it difficult to establish the full extent of the destruction. The recent attacks have compounded that damage by disabling facilities that distribute electricity between regions.
According to Ismail, areas still connected to the grid are relying on load-sharing arrangements and emergency rerouting of electricity. Some communities receive power on alternating days, while others experience prolonged scheduled and unscheduled cuts.
In parts of White Nile, North Kordofan and other areas dependent on severely damaged facilities, outages can last considerably longer.
Introducing alternative energy systems, including solar power, would reduce the dependence of hospitals and agricultural projects on the national grid. Yet those systems also require financing, equipment, and maintenance at a time when Sudan's public institutions are struggling to fund even basic repairs.
"A worrying trend is the recent intensification of drone strikes targeting power stations and fuel supply," the UN Human Rights office said this week. "The parties to the conflict must protect civilians and uphold their international law obligations--the world is watching," said UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk.
