Without your support, we can 't operate. Please consider becoming a paid subscriber or making a . | | ---|---|--- Mohammed Al-Mashkour Ali stands beside his grain mill at the Al-Lafa market in south Khartoum on November 16, 2026. Prolonged power outages following recent drone strikes on Sudan's electricity infrastructure have forced him to work alone overnight during the limited hours electricity is available. Photo by Aunnab Alman. Story by Aunnab Alman KHARTOUM, Sudan--In what has become an increasingly frequent feature of daily life in large swathes of Sudan, Afifa Mohammed spent most of Tuesday in her small home in Al-Asal south of Khartoum without electricity. The power went out at 10 a.m. and did not return until close to midnight. Like millions of other Sudanese displaced by the country's brutal civil war, Mohammed was forced to flee her hometown of Bara, North Kordofan, with her children in March. Added to the hardship of displacement, she now has to contend with a lack of electricity. She stays awake late into the night when power is available and rushes to complete tasks that require electricity--like pumping and storing water. The family now buys small quantities of food daily because they can no longer depend on refrigeration. There is no reliable schedule of power cuts. Some days, electricity comes on during the day before cutting out after sunset. Other days, the pattern is reversed. Sudan's electricity network has been severely damaged over the last three and a half years of war with civilian infrastructure being targeted by both the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF). Yet a particularly intense wave of drone strikes at the end of October and into November targeting power stations, fuel supplies, and electricity infrastructure has brought the country's power grid to the brink of collapse. The United Nations children's agency (UNICEF) recently that not a day had passed during the last week of October without a drone striking a power station in Sudan. "In just over two weeks between October 20 and November 4, 29 drone strikes, attributed to the Rapid Support Forces, hit electricity facilities and fuel stations across 11 states, triggering widespread power blackouts and further fuel shortages affecting millions far from the conflict frontlines," the United Nations Human Rights Office said in a this week. "These drone strikes had a devastating impact on civilians and essential services, causing power outages that disrupted health services including dialysis and surgical procedures, access to clean water and food production." Two weeks after the wave of attacks, major substations remain out of service. Repairing some of the country's most important power facilities could take months or longer, Shaker Ismail, an engineer with the Sudanese Electricity Company, told Drop Site News. Across parts of the country, electricity is being rationed through planned cuts that do not adhere to a regular schedule, while hospitals, water systems, farms, and businesses struggle to operate on an already weakened grid. Replacement transformers must be manufactured abroad, spare parts are scarce, and the threat of further attacks is complicating efforts to restore power. Ismail said the recent wave of attacks damaged some of the most difficult and expensive components to replace, including high-capacity transformers and digital control systems. Unlike smaller electrical equipment, the transformers cannot be purchased from local suppliers and instead must be manufactured to order in Europe or Asia to match the specifications of individual power stations. Manufacturing, shipping, and installation can take several months to more than a year, he added, particularly when equipment must be transported through a country torn apart by war. A single large transformer can cost millions of dollars while Sudan's electricity authorities face shortages of foreign currency, Ismail said. Additional shortages in essential supplies, including cables, circuit breakers, and insulating oil, have exacerbated the crisis while reserve stocks have been depleted following the destruction of major warehouses in Khartoum. The Sudanese military-backed government has accused the RSF of carrying out attacks on electricity infrastructure, and the UN also cited the RSF regarding the latest wave of strikes. While both warring parties have targeted civilians and committed human rights abuses, the RSF has been accused of the most serious crimes, including actions in the group's takeover of El Fasher in 2025 that bore "the hallmarks of genocide," according to a UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission for Sudan. The conflict erupted in April 2023 when a long simmering rivalry between the two factions exploded into fighting. At least 150,000 people have been killed, with some estimates running far higher. Some 14 million have been forced from their homes and the International Rescue Committee says more people face famine in Sudan than in the rest of the world combined. As the war between the SAF and the RSF continues to rage, the threat of renewed attacks has created another obstacle to restoring the power grid. According to Ismail, foreign companies and potential international donors are reluctant to finance repairs or send specialist engineers into areas where installations could be struck again. One of Sudan's most important power stations, the Um Dabakir thermal power plant in White Nile State, was badly damaged in an October 29 strike that forced it to shut down. The station supplied major parts of White Nile and North Kordofan states, supported the wider grid serving Khartoum and Al-Jazirah, and provided electricity used by water-treatment facilities, hospitals, and agricultural projects, Ismail said. Communities around Kosti, Rabak, and Al-Obeid, including large numbers of people displaced by the war, depend on services connected to the affected network. Restoring the station would require four replacement main transformers, reconstruction of its control room and electrical feeders, and maintenance of three damaged generating units, according to Ismail. He estimated that the repairs would cost tens of millions of dollars and take at least several months. | | ---|---|--- Workers assess damage at the Al-Markhiyat power station north of Omdurman on October 28, 2026, following a drone strike on October 27. Photo by Ebrahim Hamid / AFP via Getty Images. In Khartoum, the Al-Markhiyat substation west of Omdurman was also put out of service following a strike on October 27. The facility is a major connection point for electricity transmitted from Merowe Dam to Omdurman, Bahri, and parts of the capital. Its disruption also affected water infrastructure and hospitals connected to the network. Initial estimates suggested repairs could be completed within 10 days. But Ismail said the damage required imported transformers, high-voltage insulators, and other equipment unavailable locally. Affected areas continued to experience prolonged outages and scheduled power cuts as of this week. The Sudan Electricity Holding Company and Ministry of Energy have yet to publicly announce the restoration of the major facilities damaged in the attacks. On November 15, distribution transformers were installed to restore supplies to Khartoum's Central Market and Local Market. But these localized interventions have not resolved the wider damage to the transmission network. Effects Ranging from Dialysis to Agriculture At Abdullah Sheikh Al-Jumaih Hospital in Dongola, Northern State, power cuts have interrupted patients during dialysis treatment. Dr. Rasha Abdullah, a physician at the hospital, told Drop Site that a power cut in early November caused at least one dialysis machine's electrically powered blood pump to stop functioning, leaving blood in the tubing and filter at risk of clotting before it could be returned to the patient. Abdullah scrambled to use the machine's manual emergency mechanism to return the blood to the patient's circulation. "The medical situation in the Northern State is critical, as hospitals rely on electricity for up to 98 per cent of their equipment and lighting," Abdullah said. She added that the power cuts have also disrupted the hospital's medicine storage. | | ---|---|--- Haemodialysis machines inside the Al-Asil Center in Dongola, Northern State, Sudan on November 19, 2026. During sudden power cuts this month when backup power failed, medical staff were forced to manually hand-crank the machines' blood pumps to return circulating blood to patients before it clotted, while power outages also forced the center to discard refrigerated stocks of essential anti-clotting heparin. Photo courtesy of Dr. Rasha Abdullah. During one prolonged outage, the hospital's refrigeration systems stopped functioning for an entire day. With no alternative available, staff were forced to discard quantities of heparin, a medication used to prevent blood clotting during dialysis, because they could no longer ensure that the affected supplies had been stored under the proper conditions, Abdullah said. Attacks on power infrastructure are also disrupting water supplies. "The right to water deteriorated significantly, particularly as prolonged electricity cuts, fuel shortages, attacks on infrastructure and disruptions to water-pumping systems affected access to safe drinking water," the UN Human Rights Office said in a recent report. Workers and farmers across the economy are being affected by repeated blackouts. At Al-Lafa market, south of Khartoum, grain mill owner Mohammed Al-Mashkour Ali said that after the recent wave of attacks, electricity in his area was available only between midnight and 7 a.m. He has taken to working alone at night, grinding as much grain as possible before customers arrived the following day. "During the day, the electricity is completely cut off," Ali said. "Customers come to buy grain and have it ground, but I am unable to meet their demands." He initially tried using a small generator, but rising fuel prices made it too expensive to operate. "In the early days, I tried relying on a small generator, but the rise in fuel prices caused me financial losses with little return, so I stopped," he said. In Al-Jazirah State, farmer Sahar Mohammed said electricity shortages had disrupted the processing of agricultural products, even in areas where irrigation does not depend directly on the national grid. Mills and oil-processing facilities rely on electricity, while the cost of operating diesel-powered alternatives has increased. In Northern State, farmer Abu al-Qasim Muhammad Ahmad said the shutdown of the Al-Daba substation had left his area on an alternating electricity schedule: one day with power, followed by one day without it. He said the irregular pumping has damaged his alfalfa and orange crops. Farmers who switched to diesel-powered irrigation faced higher costs and fuel shortages. Ahmad estimated that his production costs had doubled. He feared that continued disruptions would affect preparations for the winter growing season, particularly for crops of wheat and fava beans. Sudan's electricity network had suffered extensive damage before the intense wave of drone strikes that began in late October. Before the latest attacks, national generation capacity had fallen from approximately 4,400 megawatts before the war to around 1,100 megawatts, according to the Associated Press. Merowe Dam is now the last major power source in the country, providing more than 70% of the country's electricity and making transmission facilities that distribute its output to other parts of the country even more critical. Ismail estimated that approximately 70% of Sudan's electricity infrastructure had been affected by the conflict and that the cost of repairing the wider network could exceed $3 billion, though he warned the lack of comprehensive records made it difficult to establish the full extent of the destruction. The recent attacks have compounded that damage by disabling facilities that distribute electricity between regions. According to Ismail, areas still connected to the grid are relying on load-sharing arrangements and emergency rerouting of electricity. Some communities receive power on alternating days, while others experience prolonged scheduled and unscheduled cuts. In parts of White Nile, North Kordofan and other areas dependent on severely damaged facilities, outages can last considerably longer. Introducing alternative energy systems, including solar power, would reduce the dependence of hospitals and agricultural projects on the national grid. Yet those systems also require financing, equipment, and maintenance at a time when Sudan's public institutions are struggling to fund even basic repairs. "A worrying trend is the recent intensification of drone strikes targeting power stations and fuel supply," the UN Human Rights office said this week. "The parties to the conflict must protect civilians and uphold their international law obligations--the world is watching," said UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk. body:

Tell the EPA: Put People Before Corporate Profits!

Trump’s EPA is proposing to make it even easier for the oil and gas industry to
spew methane pollution into our communities — it’s bad for our health, our
climate, and our wallets.

This latest attack on common-sense safeguards against harmful methane gas
pollution endangers communities, makes us sick, jacks up our energy bills, and
worsens the climate crisis. It benefits Trump’s corporate cronies while everyday
people foot the bill.

We won’t stand for it. We have until December 16 to voice opposition to this dangerous rollback.

Tell the EPA: Protect us from harmful methane gas pollution! https://links.messages.lcv. ADD YOUR NAME https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/KybpT- Peter, Trump’s EPA is proposing to roll back limits on methane gas pollution for the
oil and gas industry — bad for our health, our climate, and our wallets. Weakening the 2024 Methane Rule would eliminate common-sense safeguards against
the dangers of methane gas waste. On top of the long-known health and climate
harm that methane pollution causes, it would also drive up costs for families
who are already struggling with high energy bills, allowing for more reckless
leaks and waste of methane — with everyday people footing the bill. Speak out against methane gas pollution! https://links.messages.lcv. TAKE ACTION NOW https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/3Z0ec- More methane gas in our environment will expose our communities to even more
unnecessary, dangerous air pollution, harming public health and exacerbating the
climate crisis, all so that Big Polluters can rake in even more profits. Trump
and EPA Administrator Zeldin are making it crystal clear that they’re willing to
sell out the health and safety of our families and environment in order to
reward their buddies in the oil and gas industry. The EPA must reverse course and start doing its job by protecting the
environment and putting the American people’s interests ahead of billionaire Big
Polluters. Add your name and urge the EPA to do its job >> https://links.messages.lcv. Thank you for joining LCV to stand up for the health of our families and the
environment. Lizzy Duncan

---
|
---
Dear Friend, This week, a Wyoming story became a national story, and the Freedom Caucus movement is the reason. The Wyoming Freedom Caucus led the way, our Network took it national, and now state senators are being asked to answer for it. We also have news from Texas, Alabama, and Montana. Here's what your support made possible this week.
---
|
---
**WYOMING**
---
Ahead of the elections, the **Wyoming Freedom Caucus** warned voters about liberal Republican Eric Barlow, and Wyoming elected him governor anyway.Now Gov.-elect Barlow has nominated Walter Eggers, a lifelong Democrat, to be Attorney General. WYFC's Chip Neiman broke the story in an op-ed titled "The Wyoming Senate Must Reject Walter Eggers as Attorney General." FEC records show Eggers gave $18,735 to the Wyoming Democratic Party, plus checks to Obama, Clinton, Biden, and Harris.

The State Freedom Caucus Network followed Chip's lead and took the story national. Our post (below) passed half a million views, The Federalist [covered it](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjo14OgpGP35sI5vBCzgz-2Fk7MdvkiKopYQ0G84TFFcfgo3nELsAD2H6rKhHafmHGF0qB4UQ0OscfceDgiymWUV-2Bt1SJwIvbyWlfIf32OVVvo02BpLord3Nq0DMMqvggFAF6ve22Gpqq83iUGT-2Bt92hU4MdTQSEm8ATv-2BsOrXfhZ4IZry9_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerWYMbAJhIleKmyUWW8diNSpKz5LU5sweRMsVvsZzylsBzJ0ZJ30G1kJILiNeUS2JA4RdcD0EZgFojVmfm5EITQ1hhVhsKwXbX3BK6EshMYKzNR9RyAT37DDfmoSk0G5282m7aPY2HnOx6-2Fz6t8hhVbCYcNnh1R-2FoxDVyx5KhS7FVBjrJ0xUOWiiHzGRb-2F2nFlXlvbM6SPKiNk8BFgkFRtPPTLnsxOkJ-2BDh-2BtNlOsE9lQ-3D) and embedded our post, and our review of all 12 Republican governors-elect found Barlow is the only one who named a Democrat to a top post. It's simply unacceptable that the reddest state in the country has a liberal attorney general.

Thankfully, the pressure is working. Cowboy State Daily reached 15 of the 29 Republican state senators. Three said no, one said yes, and most are undecided. Senate leadership has not commented. When one senator said none of them are ready to "bow to the will of the Freedom Caucus," the answer is simple: this isn't about the Freedom Caucus. It's about honoring the voters who elected a Republican governor and a Republican Senate.

| Friend, [There is no gentle way to say it, so I won’t try: _**Republicans got crushed on Election Day.**_](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyMkkGP2yAUhH8NvhHBw4Bz8KGqFamH7SnaHhGBtw6qDRZgb_vvK5K0596seaNvxiN-vJk3G5YQ5-92xdEdweRi6h0zup8phjgbYKAo5xSYsa6GA01vOz86rwR0OHJ9lsCYENDdR3vjwLweBONKqtuH4gOXmknAM8pB6S6MDcc5MD70EoYTU0wLDbZ31t-kdqRn--ZtxXJyKRbMh22ZIcbUvlI8ubR2y3ivdStEfCFwIXAp6PaMp88QM_rmIHCJuTgCl0f9LZVKcUHXCLTs-cDfNM4hzjm4O0W62QYSl72uZkUf9pWICVcbFgKqiSXt2SERU4LVNPdDrY6I6ev7N6Cv3-Kvg7PrZsMciZjapeX_jX-mu7yXO3oaZ_Ovh3lWfgJSrBgrEdPHHn22oYQ4E1B2rVsqoYGImPqn0hMxccYIqNyGyM0qppp3JKDwl6nBv4pwzpW5Xun79cS57oezqcAG2Q89lVp2efTbZ1iWUJQmPZvbAI_B6_8_jWOEPwEAAP__9fPCQQ) To put it in historical terms, last week’s GOP defeat is the seventh-largest midterm defeat since 1938, when Franklin Delano Roosevelt’s Democrats took the worst midterm beating of the modern era. Today, I'm proud to join forces with Stand in the Gap, a non-profit organization dedicated to supporting the patriots who exercised their First Amendment rights in protest of the outcome of that election. I want to reach as many people as I can with this request... I told their founder, Shane Jenkins, that I would help him raise $20,000 before the end of the month to help Stand in the Gap provide help, hope, and healing to the January 6th patriots. Even a donation of $10 can give a January 6th patriot the support they need. Otherwise, let me explain why I 'm asking you to donate at least $10: $10 because the " crime" these patriots committed was fighting for their country. $10 because even though they've been pardoned, many of them are struggling to get back on their feet. $10 because Stand in the Gap is providing them with the resources they need to successfully reintegrate into their communities, find work, reconnect with family, and restore their rights. Not only are these men and women patriots, but they come from all walks of life -- law enforcement, veterans, white-collar professionals, blue-collar workers, and all races and religions. And they were hunted down in a political persecution that denied them their constitutional rights. Stand in the Gap exists to provide real, practical help, like rent money, job training, transportation, legal referrals, trauma counseling, and health insurance, to help these persecuted patriots move on with their lives. Your gift today can help one of these patriots find the help, hope, and healing they need to succeed in their second chance. * **Mixed analyst views:** Seaport assigned neutral, citing the valuation leap and growth needs, while William Blair set outperform on efficiency and long-term profitability potential.

Bitcoin **[plunged below $60,000 Friday,](https://substack.com/redirect/019617a0-e13d-4aa0-8916-4bc5fd6c816b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** down 23% in November and on track for its **[worst month since June 2022,](https://substack.com/redirect/7497e3c9-a960-44c8-916e-f076f880456a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/7497e3c9-a960-44c8-916e-f076f880456a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)as capital rotated toward major IPOs and the coin tracked risk assets rather than hedging them.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/01b6daa4-d809-4c77-8819-dd45ff644bd7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Pre-IPO pattern repeats:** It dropped 22.7% in the 30 days before Anthropic's debut and 22.3% ahead of SpaceX's June listing, with ether falling similarly.
* **ETF outflows add pressure:** U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs saw roughly $3.5 billion in net withdrawals this month, including $582 million Thursday.
* **Fails digital-gold test:** Experts note rising correlation with the Nasdaq-100 and stocks, **[as gold itself fell over 35% from its 2026 peak](https://substack.com/redirect/0d07e22c-134b-4c60-a2b6-ceee2abcc47e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** amid higher rates.
* **Support range in focus:** Analysts flag $60,000-$62,000 as critical; a break could retest the July low near $57,737 while corporate treasuries and DATs amplify swings.
[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/88de1fdc-5f7a-4192-b7e8-13b843e00c07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* * *
# [SanDisk sinks after its 8-for-1 split as chips get crushed](https://substack.com/redirect/01b6daa4-d809-4c77-8819-dd45ff644bd7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
SanDisk stock began trading Friday on an **[8-for-1 split basis near $88](https://substack.com/redirect/94287bfb-83dd-4f23-b586-af4ec08bb05f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after closing above $755 Thursday, falling 7% premarket as the broader semiconductor sector declined.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/01b6daa4-d809-4c77-8819-dd45ff644bd7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Split mechanics clear:** Shareholders received seven additional shares for each held as of Nov. 9; total holdings value is unchanged.
* **Peers also lower:** Seagate and Western Digital were set to open down, with Micron off 2% and SK Hynix down 4%.
* **AI infrastructure pressure:** The move came as the AI infrastructure trade faced selling after Anthropic's debut.
* **Adjusted pricing only:** The split reduces the per-share price to one-eighth of the prior level without altering company fundamentals.

[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/88de1fdc-5f7a-4192-b7e8-13b843e00c07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

# [Apple quietly pulls AI agent job listing as Ternus accelerates](https://substack.com/redirect/01b6daa4-d809-4c77-8819-dd45ff644bd7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Lede:** Apple removed a job listing Friday for an AI agent that browses the web, works across apps and writes code, **[signaling CEO John Ternus is pushing faster](https://substack.com/redirect/23e4863d-0f1e-45ad-8e7c-5ffe3f1874ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after Meta's Muse and Anthropic gained App Store traction.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/01b6daa4-d809-4c77-8819-dd45ff644bd7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Listing details and removal:** Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported the agent description before Apple killed the post, typical when plans leak.
* **Ternus timeline and pressure:** CEO since Sept. 1, Ternus has pressed software chief Craig Federighi; a launch is targeted as soon as late next year.
* **Market reaction immediate:** Anthropic fell nearly 5% late Thursday, Meta about 1%, while Apple rose and held up better than the Nasdaq 100 Friday.
* **Spending contrast sharp:** Apple's capex fell nearly 30% to about $9 billion last fiscal year while Microsoft, Meta, Alphabet and Amazon spent more than $600 billion; Apple rents Gemini for roughly $1 billion annually.
[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/88de1fdc-5f7a-4192-b7e8-13b843e00c07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* * *
# [Verizon CEO: SpaceX needs $300 billion to match our network](https://substack.com/redirect/01b6daa4-d809-4c77-8819-dd45ff644bd7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Verizon CEO Dan Schulman said Elon Musk **[would need four to six years and about $300 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/29635940-4c8a-4678-b762-69a2dd0c3c66?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for Starlink to field a U.S. mobile network essentially identical to Verizon's, becoming only the sixth entrant.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b53f9ce3-039b-4629-ac50-f986a1901ba2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **No structural edge claimed:** Schulman told Fortune there is "no secret sauce" or cost advantage; the result would be a conventional network years from now.
* **Recent spectrum and plans:** SpaceX acquired spectrum from Echostar in a $17 billion deal and plans micro cell towers as early as next year; last month's carrier announcement cut $50 billion from major telecom market caps.
* **Starlink scale today:** With 12 million paying subscribers, Starlink is SpaceX's only profitable arm.
* **Market already competitive:** Schulman expects the industry to look "radically different" in three or four years amid 6G and AI fabric, with or without SpaceX.
[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/88de1fdc-5f7a-4192-b7e8-13b843e00c07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* * *
# [Johnson's Social Security plan labeled "generational theft"](https://substack.com/redirect/01b6daa4-d809-4c77-8819-dd45ff644bd7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Sen. Ron Johnson's Stop Scaring Seniors Act would **[cover Social Security shortfalls with Treasury borrowing](https://substack.com/redirect/f20a42f8-5344-41b4-9dab-2a10f2bed6af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to avoid a 22% cut, drawing immediate "generational theft" criticism and a $190 trillion debt warning.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/01b6daa4-d809-4c77-8819-dd45ff644bd7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Bill mechanics simple:** It authorizes transfers from the general fund to the Old-Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance Trust Fund once reserves are depleted, keeping full benefits without tax hikes or cuts.
* **Debt estimates stark:** CRFB projects $190 trillion in added debt over 75 years in inflation-adjusted terms, or 165% of GDP; Jessica Riedl put a $45 trillion figure on the first three decades.
* **Expert reactions sharp:** Douglas Holtz-Eakin called it "anti-reform" and "a terrible step in the wrong direction"; Maya MacGuineas said it would explode the debt and risk a crisis.
* **Johnson 's defense:** He said the bill "simply prevents Social Security benefits from being reduced when the trust fund is depleted," arguing the broader deficit must be addressed.

November 20, 2026
Our ruling class and corporate media are so upset that Donald Trump is president that it is only a matter of time until he is blamed for the Peloponnesian War. If you pointed out to a Trump hater that this war was fought 2,300 years ago, he would respond, "Yeah. But Trump's distant ancestor caused it."

We see this thinking in [blaming Trump](https://substack.com/redirect/c1b3e6ba-1ac4-42c3-98cf-718a0d0170c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and his HHS (Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr. (RFK Jr.) for recent increase in measles.

Unlike most doctors, I have seen many cases of measles because I spent a year as a volunteer physician in Haiti when I was a young man.

[ Measles](https://substack.com/redirect/a30b0a97-b42e-4c8b-896b-551dbea75859?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), also called Rubeola, is highly contagious because the causative virus becomes airborne when an infected patient coughs or sneezes. This disease typically lasts 7-10 days and his characterized by a cough, red eyes, runny nose, a rash and fever. Diarrhea is common and in rare cases, brain and testicular swelling can occur.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/47785cec-9d3c-4914-88f2-f43544dda15b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A case of measles in a child

In the United States, measles is fatal in about 1 of 1000 cases.

But this was not the case in Haiti. Infected infants were often severely malnourished and developed diarrhea that could not be countered with intravenous hydration because the infant's vascular system had collapsed. The result was death.

Fortunately, measles can easily be prevented with a vaccine and a booster which are 97% effective. Since the virus rarely mutates, this vaccine is effective in most patients for life.
Because of vaccination, measles was declared eliminated in the United States by the WHO (World Health Organization). But now measles has become more common with 5,400 cases reported in the United States in 2025. Thus, the WHO has revoked the elimination status.

But the question is why did this happen? If you read the propaganda of the corporate media, it is because RFK Jr. discouraged vaccination. But this simply is not true. He never said that American citizens did should not get the measles vaccine. It is true that he has questioned the wisdom of other vaccines, but not the measles vaccine.

President Trump did advocate giving measles as a single vaccine rather the employing the present vaccine that combines measles with rubella and mumps (MMR). But this never became public policy.

Furthermore, the resurgence of measles is an [international phenomenon](https://substack.com/redirect/999465ae-7dfc-4620-9cb2-a8dbc8268f5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). If one assumes that President Trump and RFK Jr. are responsible for the resurgence of measles, why did [Canada](https://substack.com/redirect/36039f27-7c98-4e69-93fb-810db0803db0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and England also lose their elimination status? Do the English and Canadians follow the vaccination advice of President Trump?

Afterall, the English did replace the statue Admiral Horatio Nelson with one of Donald Trump in Trafalgar Square. And Canada replaced King Charles III's visage with that of Donald Trump on its postage stamps and currency.

But the readers who suspect I fabricated the previous paragraph, are now wondering why this happened in England and Canada too. And that reason is obvious: the massive increase of immigrants into these countries who were carriers of measles.

It is not a coincidence that the first increase in measles was seen in [Texas](https://substack.com/redirect/fa9a5207-e432-49a2-a5ae-ccb4b2288115?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the port of entry where the Biden administration allowed illegals to flood the country.

And the media made a big deal about Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro' s press conference where he blamed President Trump for three deaths caused by measles in Lancaster County.

But I went to medical school at Hershey (Penn State) which is near Lancaster County, and I will never forget seeing a horrible fatal case of tetanus, a disease easily preventable with vaccination.

And why was this patient not vaccinated? Because he was Amish and some Amish sects refuse vaccination. Yet the statement released by Governor Shapiro refused to address whether those deaths occurred in Amish patients because of "[privacy](https://substack.com/redirect/3dafcf33-6b8e-4f70-a925-00d13262b411?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" concerns.

And another third world disease is increasing rapidly in the [United States, England and Canada](https://substack.com/redirect/02da0887-2134-4a22-96fb-324ca75fff2a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - tuberculosis. Yet the corporate media is not mentioning this. Why? Because there is no effective vaccine for tuberculosis and President Trump and RFK Jr. can't be blamed for its resurgence.

But one thing is for sure. If some future historian determines that Sparta conquered Athens because of a measles epidemic, it will surely be the fault of President Trump's distant ancestor.

body:
Horse country, more room for local care, and two short videos on what comes next for property taxes.

Ryan Chamberlin for State Representative

https://clicks.aweber.com/y/ct/?l=1fqto&m=iISkBlttCM5liyD&b=OdNsZ2Si9rpiyAuFCzNVhg

DISTRICT 24 NEWSLETTER

NOVEMBER 20, 2026

FROM RYAN’S DESK

Good things are happening close to home
Friends and Neighbors,
There’s a lot to be proud of in Marion County this week. At the Horse Farms Forever Conservation Summit, I got to spend time with Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson and thank the people working to keep our horse farms and ranches here for the next generation.

And there’s good news in Ocala. The Estella Byrd Whitman Community Health Center is expanding! I’m grateful to Senator Stan McClain and the center’s team for working with me to help secure state funding. More room to care for our neighbors is something worth celebrating.
I’ve also been asking a question I hear from people across the district. Where are our tax dollars going? I’ve pulled together this week’s updates, including two short videos, so you can hear what I’m asking of local officials and see what comes next.
God bless,
Ryan Chamberlin

NOVEMBER 12 · OCALA

Keeping Marion County’s horse country alive
Ryan Chamberlin and Florida Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson at the Horse Farms Forever summit

https://clicks.aweber.com/y/ct/?l=1fqto&m=iISkBlttCM5liyD&b=WTO.XgEgMUOBID8HG9R1Aw

Horse Farms Forever’s annual Conservation Summit brought people together to talk about protecting the farms, ranches and open spaces that are part of Marion County’s heritage. I appreciated the chance to speak with Commissioner Simpson and thank him for his work on conservation in Florida.
See the summit photo →

https://clicks.aweber.com/y/ct/?l=1fqto&m=iISkBlttCM5liyD&b=WTO.XgEgMUOBID8HG9R1Aw

NOVEMBER 13 UPDATE · OCALA

Good news for local health care
Community partners outside the Estella Byrd Whitman Community Health Center

https://clicks.aweber.com/y/ct/?l=1fqto&m=iISkBlttCM5liyD&b=RHVsyY_2CoqtOR9il4cXEw

The Estella Byrd Whitman Community Health Center is expanding. It was an honor to work with Senator Stan McClain and the center to help secure state funding. I appreciate the staff and community partners working to make care more accessible here in Marion County.
See the health center update →

https://clicks.aweber.com/y/ct/?l=1fqto&m=iISkBlttCM5liyD&b=RHVsyY_2CoqtOR9il4cXEw

PROPERTY TAX UPDATE

What comes next after Amendment 3?
I’ve shared several updates this week about where Florida goes after Amendment 3. They cover the cost of owning a home, what property taxes mean for small businesses, and what local budgets should show residents before officials consider new fees or reductions to services.
My proposal is to review county spending, work toward replacing property tax revenue, and protect funding for essential services such as public safety and schools. The links below take you to each update.

| | | This week, on national radio, former Republican LG nominee E.W. Jackson attacked me for taking my oath of office as Virginia’s Lieutenant Governor, declaring that swearing in on the Qur’an is “no different” than swearing in on the “Satanic Bible” and calling Allah a “demonic pagan deity.”
**Let’s be clear about what this is: unvarnished, dangerous bigotry and hate speech.**
When I took the oath of office in January as the first Muslim woman elected to statewide office in American history, I did so in the Commonwealth in which Thomas Jefferson wrote the Virginia Statute for Religious Freedom — a foundational promise that no person’s faith or religious identity disqualifies them from serving their neighbors or being recognized as American.
I ran for office to bring a new kind of leadership to Virginia: leadership rooted in dignity, inclusion, and delivering real results for working families — not tearing communities apart to score cheap points on right-wing talk radio.
When extremist voices use their platforms to dehumanize Muslim Americans and attack religious freedom, they aren’t just attacking me. They are attacking the very idea of a Virginia — and an America — where everyone belongs.
**I will never back down from this kind of hate. And I need you standing with me.**
Right-wing extremists are already gearing up to target our progress and undermine the historic coalition we built across Virginia. We need the resources to fight back, defend our values, and keep building an inclusive Commonwealth. **[Will you rush $10, $25, or $50 right now to stand against bigotry and power our fight forward?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143789124/661384795/-2059200927?refcode=261120em&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85MzMwMCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZGViOThmMS0xOWU1LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=C8IIRm_Y3qb-46Qsd9QgtAqQshwYedwTphixOOMsEHU=)**

clean_body: Help me stand up for freedom of faith | | | | = | | | This week, on national radio, former Republican LG nominee E.W. Jackson attacked me for taking my oath of office as Virginia’s Lieutenant Governor, declaring that swearing in on the Qur’an is “no different” than swearing in on the “Satanic Bible” and calling Allah a “demonic pagan deity.” Let’s be clear about what this is: unvarnished, dangerous bigotry and hate speech. When I took the oath of office in January as the first Muslim woman elected to statewide office in American history, I did so in the Commonwealth in which Thomas Jefferson wrote the Virginia Statute for Religious Freedom — a foundational promise that no person’s faith or religious identity disqualifies them from serving their neighbors or being recognized as American. I ran for office to bring a new kind of leadership to Virginia: leadership rooted in dignity, inclusion, and delivering real results for working families — not tearing communities apart to score cheap points on right-wing talk radio. When extremist voices use their platforms to dehumanize Muslim Americans and attack religious freedom, they aren’t just attacking me. They are attacking the very idea of a Virginia — and an America — where everyone belongs. I will never back down from this kind of hate. And I need you standing with me. Right-wing extremists are already gearing up to target our progress and undermine the historic coalition we built across Virginia. We need the resources to fight back, defend our values, and keep building an inclusive Commonwealth. = = Hate has no home in Virginia. Thank you for having my back. body:
A new bipartisan framework →| | | |
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143791186/661391477/639067025?refcode=261120em_sjj_safety&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ZjdjMDE0Ni0xZmU1LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=xjK0wrUTi5P2dwBcSD4tgSO2oyDpS2i-VhRUsMSGlx0=)
---
Things are continuing to move quickly on AI development, and the risks are escalating fast. From earlier this fall when rogue AI agents targeted the websites of foreign nations, to just this week when they hacked into Americans’ bank accounts, it’s clear that Congress must act — so let me share what we’re doing to rein in AI right now. We just launched a new bipartisan group in the House called the **AI Safety and Innovation Caucus. ** Together, we’ll work to create safeguards for AI while ensuring America remains a leader in the global AI space. A part of this work is responding quickly when AI incidents and breaches happen, keeping the public informed, and helping shape and strengthen the AI legislation Congress takes up. Which brings me to my next update: yesterday, I teamed up with Reps. Celeste Maloy of Utah and Don Beyer of Virginia to release the outline of the _SAFE AI Act_ , which will create real, bipartisan guardrails for the most powerful AI systems.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143791187/661391478/1267180059?contactdata=HjW8z4JPHZThAWjo/IXZwoOV3/wSdb2QLLe0jjoC11S2iADkOD0QV9X48xKUprDrkvRrsKlz88Wl76lK/2OxPn2abcN1daW0SavDL6P349swMFqOBE7Qe6vjRsPq8MUeRnchnZHLLnyQa1dmnZguaQ==&refcode=261120em_sjj_safety&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ZjdjMDE0Ni0xZmU1LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=xjK0wrUTi5P2dwBcSD4tgSO2oyDpS2i-VhRUsMSGlx0=&emci=74de7ffe-18e5-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=5f7c0146-1fe5-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=14239920)
---
Right now, the companies building the most powerful AI in the world basically write their own rules. They decide how to test their models, what counts as “safe,” and what to tell the public when something goes wrong — which has been happening more and more frequently in recent weeks. Look, I don’t think ANY industry should get to police itself — but AI, which touches our public safety, our critical infrastructure, our national security, and nearly every single system we rely on as a society, certainly shouldn’t be the exception. Our bill would:
* Require frontier AI labs to build genuine safety frameworks and show their work before their systems go into wide use
* Mandate that companies report incidents and be transparent about what their models are doing
* Back it up with strong government oversight, the ability to cite civil penalties for violations, and targeted emergency authority to stop a dangerous model when it poses a serious and immediate threat
* Set a floor, not a ceiling, so states like California can go even further to protect their communities
* And adapt as the technology changes, so your safety never depends on a company keeping its word

**I’ve spent the last several years working hard on legislation to address the transformative AI landscape because I knew there would be a time when Congress would need to act urgently and with authority. I believe that moment is now. ** **[If you believe AI companies should not be allowed to “self police,” and instead should face safety regulations and government oversight, add your name to support the SAFE AI Act.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143791188/661391479/1267180059?contactdata=HjW8z4JPHZThAWjo/IXZwoOV3/wSdb2QLLe0jjoC11S2iADkOD0QV9X48xKUprDrkvRrsKlz88Wl76lK/2OxPn2abcN1daW0SavDL6P349swMFqOBE7Qe6vjRsPq8MUeRnchnZHLLnyQa1dmnZguaQ==&refcode=261120em_sjj_safety&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ZjdjMDE0Ni0xZmU1LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=xjK0wrUTi5P2dwBcSD4tgSO2oyDpS2i-VhRUsMSGlx0=&emci=74de7ffe-18e5-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=5f7c0146-1fe5-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=14239920) **

clean_body: A new bipartisan framework →| | | | = Things are continuing to move quickly on AI development, and the risks are escalating fast. From earlier this fall when rogue AI agents targeted the websites of foreign nations, to just this week when they hacked into Americans’ bank accounts, it’s clear that Congress must act — so let me share what we’re doing to rein in AI right now. We just launched a new bipartisan group in the House called the AI Safety and Innovation Caucus. Together, we’ll work to create safeguards for AI while ensuring America remains a leader in the global AI space. A part of this work is responding quickly when AI incidents and breaches happen, keeping the public informed, and helping shape and strengthen the AI legislation Congress takes up. Which brings me to my next update: yesterday, I teamed up with Reps. Celeste Maloy of Utah and Don Beyer of Virginia to release the outline of the SAFE AI Act , which will create real, bipartisan guardrails for the most powerful AI systems. Right now, the companies building the most powerful AI in the world basically write their own rules. They decide how to test their models, what counts as “safe,” and what to tell the public when something goes wrong — which has been happening more and more frequently in recent weeks. Look, I don’t think ANY industry should get to police itself — but AI, which touches our public safety, our critical infrastructure, our national security, and nearly every single system we rely on as a society, certainly shouldn’t be the exception. Our bill would: Require frontier AI labs to build genuine safety frameworks and show their work before their systems go into wide use Mandate that companies report incidents and be transparent about what their models are doing Back it up with strong government oversight, the ability to cite civil penalties for violations, and targeted emergency authority to stop a dangerous model when it poses a serious and immediate threat Set a floor, not a ceiling, so states like California can go even further to protect their communities And adapt as the technology changes, so your safety never depends on a company keeping its word I’ve spent the last several years working hard on legislation to address the transformative AI landscape because I knew there would be a time when Congress would need to act urgently and with authority. I believe that moment is now. ** This is just the beginning, and the window to get this right is right now. name: Mark Kelly
subject: This wasn’t what I had in mind
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Mark Kelly for Senate
body:
I definitely didn’t intend to end up in court against the Secretary of Defense after spending 25 years in the Navy and NASA.
#

Friend --
It’s hard to tell what you’re getting yourself into at the start of something. Gabby and I knew things were going to change when I ran for Senate, and we know more than most how public service can change your life.
We didn’t expect things to go like this, though. Getting attacked by the richest guy on Earth wasn’t on my to-do list, and neither was having the President of the United States call for my arrest and execution. And I definitely didn’t intend to end up in court against the Secretary of Defense after spending 25 years in the Navy and NASA.
But when Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth came after me, they came after the free speech rights of millions of retired veterans, too. They were trying to intimidate people into silence, to stop them from speaking out. After all those years in service, I couldn’t let that stand.
It was a year ago today that all of this started, when Trump tried to brand me a traitor, and it isn’t over yet. We’ve got a decision in this case coming. We don’t know when, and we’ll find out when everyone else does.
But I do know the only reason we’ve made it this far is because of this team. You’ve been with me for a long time, and you haven’t backed down. That means a lot to me, really.
I’ve always been willing to fight for our democracy, but it gives me a lot of hope to know that I’m not in this alone.
[**And as we wait for that decision, I’m hoping I can count on you one more time. Will you make a donation to my campaign and help raise the resources we'll need to fight back against whatever Trump and Hegseth throw at us?**](https://act.markkelly.com/go/1389?c0=mek-em-nov26.3Xma5G&refcode=em261120-1-MS&t=1&akid=6829%2E6688874%2Ey_2ZhC)

| | | Dear Peter, As I wrap up my final day as CEO of Ruth’s List Florida, I want to take a moment to say**thank you**.Leading this organization has been one of the great honors of my career. I've had the privilege of working alongside extraordinary women who believe deeply in the power of women's leadership and who are willing to do the hard work to make it possible. And what meaningful work it is. Every woman we help elect represents more than a victory on Election Night. She represents a new voice at the table, a new perspective in the decisions that shape our communities, and a new opportunity to improve the lives of the people she serves. From the halls of the Florida Capitol to county commissions, school boards, and city halls across our state, the impact of that leadership reaches far beyond the women whose names appear on the ballot.That's what has always made this work so special to me. We're not just helping women win elections. We're helping build a Florida where more people are heard, more communities are represented, and more women have the opportunity to lead. I'm incredibly proud of what we've accomplished together, especially the historic victories we celebrated just weeks ago. And I’m excited about what comes next for this amazing organization. Ruth's List is in exceptional hands, with a dedicated staff, a committed board, and an extraordinary community of supporters who believe in this mission — including you. I have no doubt that the remarkable woman who steps into this role next will take the organization to even greater heights. While my time as CEO is coming to an end, my commitment to Ruth's List certainly isn't. I'll continue supporting this work as a volunteer, a donor, and a proud champion of the women who are changing Florida for the better.Thank you for trusting me to be part of this mission, for the friendships we've built, and for everything we've accomplished together. The work continues — and so will my support.So this isn't goodbye. It's _see you soon_.
---
With gratitude,

clean_body: | | | | | | | Dear Peter, As I wrap up my final day as CEO of Ruth’s List Florida, I want to take a moment to saythank you.Leading this organization has been one of the great honors of my career. I've had the privilege of working alongside extraordinary women who believe deeply in the power of women's leadership and who are willing to do the hard work to make it possible. And what meaningful work it is. Every woman we help elect represents more than a victory on Election Night. She represents a new voice at the table, a new perspective in the decisions that shape our communities, and a new opportunity to improve the lives of the people she serves. From the halls of the Florida Capitol to county commissions, school boards, and city halls across our state, the impact of that leadership reaches far beyond the women whose names appear on the ballot.That's what has always made this work so special to me. We're not just helping women win elections. We're helping build a Florida where more people are heard, more communities are represented, and more women have the opportunity to lead. I'm incredibly proud of what we've accomplished together, especially the historic victories we celebrated just weeks ago. And I’m excited about what comes next for this amazing organization. Ruth's List is in exceptional hands, with a dedicated staff, a committed board, and an extraordinary community of supporters who believe in this mission — including you. I have no doubt that the remarkable woman who steps into this role next will take the organization to even greater heights. While my time as CEO is coming to an end, my commitment to Ruth's List certainly isn't. I'll continue supporting this work as a volunteer, a donor, and a proud champion of the women who are changing Florida for the better.Thank you for trusting me to be part of this mission, for the friendships we've built, and for everything we've accomplished together. The work continues — and so will my support.So this isn't goodbye. It's see you soon. With gratitude, Christina DiamondCEO, Ruth's List Florida P.S. While he was spending **nearly** **half a billion dollars** to boost Trump and MAGA Republicans during the midterms, a law firm linked to Musk started an "election integrity" organization called the Association of State and Local Election Officials. And Cleta Mitchell? The State Party will provide the most important facts - a kernel of truth - from the week. = ** New Democratic Legislators Sworn In! Indiana’s newest Democratic legislators were sworn in earlier this week at the Statehouse! A total of 24 new Democratic members were sworn in across the House and Senate. There are now 61 Democrats serving in the Indiana General Assembly, the most since the 2010 session. These new representatives campaigned to lower costs, fight corruption, and support all Hoosier families. We can’t wait to see the future they will build for Indiana when the new session begins in January! They will always put Hoosier families over special interests. Mike Braun Didn’t Get the Message, Announces Reelection Bid Gov. Braun is already one of the least popular governors in the nation and his approval continues to plummet. Under his watch, hundreds of thousands of Hoosiers have lost healthcare, electricity bills are up and public schools and childcare facilities around the state are closing their doors. closed. All while local taxes increase and he uses your tax dollars for helicopter trips to Jasper instead of living full time in Indianapolis like his predecessors. His reelection announcement earlier this week shows he’s simply not listening to Hoosiers. Indiana deserves better, and that means not giving Governor Braun another term. Each week, the State Party will highlight key policy or programs from Democrats at the Statehouse or across the state. Democrats deliver a better future for Hoosier families, and we urge you to share this information with your networks. Secretary-elect Beau Bayh Records Strongest Democratic Overperformance in the Country Secretary of State-elect Beau Bayh achieved the strongest performance of any statewide Democratic candidate in the country in this election, shifting Indiana 28 points from the 2024 election. He also became the first Democrat to win a statewide office in Indiana since 2012, along with State Comptroller-elect Jessica Bailey. Hoosiers are ready for a new Secretary of State who will clean up the office, restore trust, and put them first. Secretary-elect Bayh told , “I will just go anywhere. I’ll talk to anyone. Training sessions will be held: Saturday, November 21, 2026 from 10am to 4 pm in Greenwood Sunday, November 22, 2026 from 10am to 4pm in Kokomo Whether you’re thinking about working on a campaign, considering a future run for office, or simply interested in developing professional political fundraising skills, this training is an opportunity to learn from experienced professionals, gain practical skills, and connect with others interested in campaign work. body:
As the Trump administration’s chaos continues, I need to know your biggest priorities and concerns.
| | |
---
Friend, now that Democrats have secured majorities in both the House and Senate, it’s time to get to work. Because we have a lot of mess to clean up.
As Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth continue their war in Iran, their recklessness is endangering our troops and our national security.
As Robert F. Kennedy Jr. continues spreading misinformation and ridiculous conspiracy theories about vaccines, the U.S. just lost our measles elimination status.
As Donald Trump continues his pointless tariffs, the cost of everything keeps going up and up and up.
I could keep going, but I’d be here all day.
It’s time to end their corruption and chaos. It’s time to bring accountability for the harm they’ve inflicted on the American people. It’s time to finally get back to making progress on the issues that will make a real difference in your life.
**With so much work to do, I want to make sure that my priorities in the Senate reflect your own priorities. That’s why my team created this special digital focus group for you to share your input with me directly. Can I count on you to take a couple of minutes now to let me know your thoughts?**

## TIME Names 9-Year-Old Kid of the Year

## Dr. King's Lost 'I Have a Dream' Draft Discovered
The only known handwritten final draft of Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I Have a Dream" speech has resurfaced after more than six decades. The seven yellow notepad pages were found in a desk drawer belonging to Edward T. Clayton, one of King's [trusted aides and speechwriters](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkb2u2zAMRp_G3hhIsuOfwUMXb7drR4OxKIs3shRITIz79oX6Ct0_HOIc_vnavpADx-M3nrS4w23i0hbpKoFEKG9PtsmJpx_C_OR4lJCK2IxuM8oMoDUYteEu_KFNt3ZxRIa6lhY9znejpr5TrV_IdbMiPTycmUatp3F33UD3vsfZdlrPLS8Vp7VRRitlppubSLuH7kc9zmqmsekVWZaUb9-Jo3hy4Sd9KN_2dLZh8SKv0nS_GrM2Zr2u61ZOFl9SZIwnHnXWmLWcmAWqXmNW8QQeo70yi1AExxEDVDeB5KBOOUJ4i6cM1R2-cwEGjx8CBJsJTygvot3DhQX2FAtbymShRgIWkHeOZCG9BSTBg6CwSCVxrAQqz3rvogwuZbC0o6UCelLzNE_3oTFrmxf7ujgELkONcJzI4Z-0_P-7Pov5GwAA__8L8LAi). Clayton's widow, civil rights activist Xernona Clayton, first came across the pages in the late 1990s, tucked inside an envelope labeled "speech." Although she recognized their significance, she didn't realize they were King's handwritten final draft and [put them back in the drawer](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOpCAQwPGn0Q4Dgy5aUFxjt9deSVgZkBNlA0Syb_-FfYWvnUwm_9_8e6qn9sFf7q8-UVpnVbFRXVhzwFIwqcObaMuOH9Tp8JfLIeZikrYKKDwIYwSo0lvxNyrWG2kRAXmPkollAjqPnPa7ZHQbH9zwaZlna1BPL7EIAcgZn7TYdO9lO8cYUGCUwjzYGZl9sVEwsdAFRTdSNL7ENPyP_io72vCJN6Zhi2cf5F7KO3f8TwdrB2utdXAxmua4sNSYjiEm18FqEvkqSGOQ5igkWuLJrm8kmpiE-iR4YnKYiU3xbEPMR9utmDpY-yTNu_oQfH60LHdqH74Z5fcPvCX8BAAA__9hN4jJ). In 2024, she shared the pages with her financial manager, who worked with Christie's experts to identify the document. The draft shows King wrestling with word choice the night before the March on Washington, with crossed-out passages and edits throughout the seven pages. Notably, the famous "I have a dream" refrain does not appear. King [improvised it at the lectern](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFuhDAQQNHTQAfyDCyYwkUauk2bEg1mDJM1GNnOor19tLlCLvCf9L_u053Ey7F-0s7GrW7KLkwHX8lzzhynhyzB5Y1fTPEhx5p8SHmJ5CZU2FUAFaqJbJYnT1AuxjEjNyUb6IcbKt02qtzM3AzaAoIG3XYA1IGdoW86bLUidWtKMe8cACoEpVDXTjO4Gdoe-kEN3Bet4kVyiPV3kCNv7PwrPDnWNuylN1vOZyqajwLHAsfrumo729pSgWOkRUKBIyXJG50nH6nAcfePaolMe5VOZrtV9GOzhKMa6r4F3XRQRrOcl3gvqXvz607i_7j8_1FPg78BAAD__8-3fPw) after gospel singer Mahalia Jackson called out, "_Tell them about the dream_." The manuscript will be auctioned at Christie's on Jan. 22, 2027, and is expected to fetch more than $10 million.
## School Opens Free Clothing Boutique
Merideth Lett noticed that students at Flatwoods Elementary School in Northport, Alabama, were showing up in ill-fitting clothes. Some struggled to focus in class because their shoes were too small or their shirts pinched. Donated clothes existed, but they were [stuffed in boxes scattered around the building](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OozAUxfGngc6Rbb4LF9uky7ZbIgPHcDeGy9g3ifL2o8wrTH2ko5_-_27jzVOkY_3rd7iwhlECjwdeOUIEabzTwkE2vOHTnY41R86yJB9Gq22rjFFWj34WemI05eICYFGVcKYbGqv7utLl5jAtupnaUAF1M4dh6TrMtWm1buZ-MkNJ7nNnjNXWaG37S-hhwmTqznSDHtAVtcZCwunyn-mQDSG--Yl0mXkvo9tEzlxUfwp7Lez1BJ8Rn6mwVx_95HevELHjEJ_eKs8bc1R84sgqJEDNkWWjY1UTP4S-HlCBkwp-p0jIyljbmKoZyuSW80UxUm4_pHX3FH8I8vt4T2e_AwAA__-zaYd7). Now, he's . Ledger, who has autism, created LGM Bags, clear backpacks filled with sensory and comfort items for police officers, firefighters, and paramedics to carry on calls involving children in crisis. The idea started when Ledger's father, Sgt. JT Mann of the Prince George County Police Department in Virginia, about a missing child with autism. He used a phone video to coax the boy out of hiding. When Ledger heard the story, he wondered why first responders didn't carry comfort items to help kids like him. He used $100 of his savings to make the first four kits. Word spread. Corporations, churches, and first responder groups , helping the project expand to six states. Ledger and his family have now distributed nearly 500 kits. Dr. King's Lost 'I Have a Dream' Draft Discovered The only known handwritten final draft of Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I Have a Dream" speech has resurfaced after more than six decades. The seven yellow notepad pages were found in a desk drawer belonging to Edward T. Clayton, one of King's . Clayton's widow, civil rights activist Xernona Clayton, first came across the pages in the late 1990s, tucked inside an envelope labeled "speech." Although she recognized their significance, she didn't realize they were King's handwritten final draft and . In 2024, she shared the pages with her financial manager, who worked with Christie's experts to identify the document. The draft shows King wrestling with word choice the night before the March on Washington, with crossed-out passages and edits throughout the seven pages. Notably, the famous "I have a dream" refrain does not appear. King after gospel singer Mahalia Jackson called out, "Tell them about the dream." The manuscript will be auctioned at Christie's on Jan. 22, 2027, and is expected to fetch more than $10 million. School Opens Free Clothing Boutique Merideth Lett noticed that students at Flatwoods Elementary School in Northport, Alabama, were showing up in ill-fitting clothes. Some struggled to focus in class because their shoes were too small or their shirts pinched. Donated clothes existed, but they were . So Merideth, the school's counselor, transformed the system. She created Flatwoods Fancy and Flatwoods Fellas, a boutique-style shop inside the school where students and their families can browse clothing, shoes, accessories, and toiletries for free. The boutique is open to all students and their families, regardless of financial need. Shoppers can take their items home . In its first seven weeks, the boutique gave away 850 clothing items. "You cannot learn if your pants are cutting into your sides or your shoes are several sizes too small ," Merideth said. The boutique has also become a teaching tool. name: Tim Walz
subject: We’ve got to keep earning it
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Small Town PAC, [smalltownpac
body:
We’ve got to be there for people before we ask them to be there for us.
#
Peter,
If the only time folks hear from Democrats is when we need their vote, we’ve got a problem.
I’m proud of what we accomplished this month. But we can’t pack up after a good election and expect people to be there for us next time. **We’ve got to be there for them in between.**
I grew up in a small town where people knew who they could count on. You earned that by pitching in and keeping your word. I want folks to be able to say the same about Democrats.
**[Will you chip in $5 or whatever works for you today to help Small Town PAC keep organizing in communities too often written off and give local leaders the support to keep building?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261120-1.XKAHWd&amount=5&refcode=em20261120-1364&t=1&akid=1364%2E34582%2Ek1O5vb)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261120-1.XKAHWd&amount=5&refcode=20261120-1364&t=20&akid=1364%2E34582%2Ek1O5vb)**
We need to keep talking with folks who voted for us, folks who didn’t, and folks who aren’t convinced either party gives a damn about them. That means being willing to hear some things we might not like _and coming back anyway._
Those relationships take time. You can’t cram all that work into the last few weeks of a campaign and expect people to trust you.
Your support now keeps this work going between elections. We can’t put it on hold and expect to pick up right where we left off. We’ve got to keep at it in the places we won and the places where we still have ground to make up.
**[Let’s give the next round of Democratic candidates something to build on. Can you pitch in $5 today to help Small Town PAC keep doing the work that makes more wins possible?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261120-1.XKAHWd&amount=5&refcode=em20261120-1364&t=21&akid=1364%2E34582%2Ek1O5vb)**
Thanks for sticking with us. It makes a difference.
Tim

**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/stp-ms-em-footer?refcode=em20261120-1364-&t=22&refcode2=1364_34582_k1O5vb&akid=1364%2E34582%2Ek1O5vb)**

TODAY'S TOP STORIES

THOMPSON SCHOOL DISTRICT’S CONFIDENTIAL GENDER PLANS DRAW FEDERAL
PROBE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

The form Thompson School District uses to plan a student’s gender
support at school is marked with one word.

“Confidential.”

On Wednesday, the U.S. Department of Education announced it is
investigating the Loveland-based district, along with four others,
over policies the department said “appear to conceal information
from parents about a child’s ‘gender identity.'”

Thompson is the only Colorado district on the list. The others are in
Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Illinois and Minnesota.

A department office, the Student Privacy Policy Office, will decide
whether the districts broke two federal laws. One is the Family
Educational Rights and Privacy Act, which gives parents the right to
inspect their children’s education records. The other is the
Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment, which the department says
requires written parental consent before schools survey or evaluate
students on certain sensitive and private topics.

READ MORE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

NET MIGRATION PLUNGED 94% AND COMPANY EXITS DOUBLED ARRIVALS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_Colorado’s net migration from other states collapsed from 58,458 in
2024 to just 3,451 in 2025, a 94% drop, while public companies are
leaving the state at twice the rate they’re arriving._

*
A HISTORIC SLOWDOWN: Colorado’s average annual net migration fell
from 37,019 (2015-2019) to a net loss of 1,882 a year (2021-2025),
with 2025 marking the smallest population gain since 1990 and the
state’s first job decline since 2001 without a national recession.

*
COMPANIES ARE HEADING FOR THE EXITS: Since 2023, 27 Colorado public
companies have left the state or been acquired by outside buyers
versus just 13 arrivals, with Palantir’s move from Denver to Florida
the most visible example, and 2026 on pace for the largest net loss
since at least 2011.

*
GROWTH IS CONCENTRATING OUTSIDE DENVER’S CORE: Weld and Douglas
counties captured 46% of the state’s net migration over five years
and added the most jobs, while Denver, Arapahoe, Boulder and Jefferson
counties combined lost population through migration in 2025 after
gaining residents the year before.

Corporations and billionaires tried to buy this election. But it turns out, there are a whole lot more of us than there are of them.
Two weeks ago, Ohioans sent an undeniable message that our state is not for sale. There's a reason that all these corporations and outside spenders poured so much money into this race against me. They know I'm going to fight to hold them accountable and take on the rigged system they've been feasting on.
Our fight is just getting started, and my team is hard at work to ensure our office can get up and running so we can get to work. You're a big reason we got across the finish line, so you deserve to know the latest.
Here are my answers to some of the most common questions we've gotten over the past two weeks:
**Q: When will you be sworn in?**
> Great question!
> Senator Husted's term ends on December 15th under state law, which means I'll have to wait until mid-December to take office, at the earliest. However, the Senate has to be in session for swearing in, so if the Senate gavels out before December 15th, I won't be sworn in to office until January 3rd, the first day of the 120th Congress, with the rest of the new class of senators.
> Regardless, my team is doing whatever we can in this transition period to ensure we are ready to hit the ground running as soon as that date is confirmed so we can get to work for Ohio.
**Q: How long is this term anyway?**
> As many of you know, this was a special election for the seat vacated by JD Vance. That means this term goes until 2028, when Ohio will have another Senate election for a full six-year term.
**Q: What are your first priorities in the Senate?**
> We need to end this war, we need to end the tariffs, and we need to get rid of the corruption in Washington.
> One of the first things we are going to do is ban members of Congress from trading stocks. Working people pay for this corruption with higher utility bills, higher grocery prices, and higher drug prices. It's outrageous that members of Congress use their positions to enrich themselves, and we're going to make it illegal.
**Q: What committees do you hope to join in the Senate?**
> All across Ohio, I hear from families and farmers who are being crushed by reckless tariffs and an endless war in Iran that is driving up grocery, health care, diesel, and fertilizer prices.
> As the longest serving Ohioan on the Agriculture Committee ever, I worked across the aisle to pass bipartisan legislation that put more money back in the pockets of farmers, promoted America's energy independence, supported conservation efforts, and protected vital food assistance programs like SNAP.
> [I hope to rejoin this committee and lead the fight](https://substack.com/redirect/07982baa-4276-429f-95ba-9e073fb3b24c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for Ohio farmers, families, and rural communities, and ensure every American has the tools and resources they need to secure a more healthy and prosperous future.
> Regardless of my committee assignments, I'll be working with my colleagues to lower costs and ensure accountability for corporate America and those who put billionaires before working families.
**Q: Who do you plan to support for Senate Majority Leader?**
> Senator Schumer has led our caucus through difficult times and has the experience necessary to lead and deliver results for the American people, but I want to be clear: regardless of who becomes Majority Leader, I will hold their feet to the fire in delivering on the promises we made to voters this year to lower costs and end the war in Iran.
> I'll fight like hell to end the war. I'll fight like hell against these reckless tariffs. I will go after corruption.
> I have great respect for Senator Van Hollen and we have worked well together in the past. I'm glad we're having this debate, and I support a fair process. No matter who becomes the Senate Majority Leader, my top priority is fighting for Ohioans.
**Q: How can I get in touch with your official office?**
> Because we haven't been sworn in as Senators yet, the other Senators-elect and I do not have phone numbers or official Senate websites. Once I get sworn in (which, as you read above, would be as early as mid-December), we'll get our official office set up on day one to take your calls.
> But if you'd like to get in touch with my team in the meantime, you can respond to this post or share your feedback [at this form](https://substack.com/redirect/ec4f9e81-50d6-45dd-9d18-e35f017670f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Your input means a lot to us, and I appreciate your patience during this transition. The best ideas come from Ohio, and I always want to hear from you.
* * *
Thanks again for everything you've done. There's a lot of fight ahead, but I'm glad to have you by my side.
More soon,
Sherrod Brown
* * *
You helped me win this race, and it means the world to have you beside me in this fight. This was a special election, which means Democrats need to fight to hold onto this seat.

| | | Yesterday, the man Donald Trump picked to protect America’s voting systems was asked if January 6 was an attack. **His answer:****_“No, I don’t believe it was an attack.”_**
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143794906/661403901/-569431239?refcode=261120-CISA&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlM2ZhMDhkYS0yZGU1LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=UYtBsilmJbdt8kgcUK3iiioGu8EikFMhJKq-jQNpZtE=)

Michael LoSapio is Trump’s nominee to lead CISA, the agency that helps protect our critical infrastructure, including our elections. When a senator asked him who won the popular vote in 2020, he wouldn’t answer. And Republicans are racing to confirm him before Democrats take over Congress in January. You’d think they would have learned their lesson by now, but they haven’t. **We saw how important it was this fall that states were willing to defend their elections against interference from President Trump and his allies. Oregon knows this better than most—we built vote by mail, and we turned out at some of the highest levels, despite their best efforts to intimidate us. You have my promise that I will keep fighting to protect our elections, and that I won’t cave to their threats or lies.** **[The Trump Administration won’t stop its attacks, and that’s why I need you in my corner as we head into 2028 — can you chip in $15 right now so our campaign can keep standing up for Oregon’s elections?
